articleTitle: Measurement-as-a-Service: VNF-to-VNF Performance Measurement in Federated Testbed
abstract: In 5G and beyond, Network Function Virtualization (NFV) and Software Defined Networking (SDN) technologies enables an easy deployment of Virtualized Network Functions (VNF). However, designing and building scalable NFV infrastructure is quite challenging to adopt and making VNFs deployment on existing hardware. To understand such behaviour, the EU SoftFire project developed federated virtualization testbed for NFV/SDN experiments. This paper outlines the SoftFire Middleware framework and proposes an automated Measurement-as-a-Service (MaaS) for performing VNF-to-VNF performance metrics, such measurements can be exploited by an orchestrator to perform VNF instantiate selection.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Based Sub-Synchronous Oscillation Detection
abstract: Sub-synchronous resonance (SSR) is a problem that occurs in the modern electrical system (i.e. Generators with long-series compensated transmission lines) due to the Generator (Turbine) experiencing oscillations at different frequencies that are below their natural frequency. Various methods are used to compute the necessary conditions of SSR behavior and the eigenvalue analysis method is widely used. However, the conventional methods provide accuracy but they are not computationally efficient, and necessary steps cannot be taken immediately to mitigate the effects. This paper focuses on the implementation of a machine-learning approach for the detection of sub-synchronous resonance and its labeling.

articleTitle: A Low-cost Monitoring System for Enhanced Indoor Air Quality inside Built environment
abstract: Usage of ductless split conditioners inside built environment has seen a significant rise in tropical countries like India, as they provide thermal comfort. However, the absence of fresh air ventilation in ductless split conditioners has resulted in scenarios of CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> concentration above the ASHRAE threshold limit of $1000 \mathbf{p p m}$ for better indoor air quality and health. The study demonstrates the working principle of an IoT based automated system to provide ventilation during required periods to maintain better indoor air quality in an office type workspace. An Arduino Uno with wifi module measures the CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> concentration through a CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> sensor connected to it and transfers the data onto an online platform for data logging. Once the CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> concentration attains the upper limit, the system triggers the exhaust fan to provide fresh air ventilation until the CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> concentration decays to a preset lower limit. The results indicate that the automated system can be implemented to measure and maintain the average CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> concentration below 1000 ppm over a period of 8 hours.

articleTitle: Ergonomic Risk Management Using Machine Learning and Virtual Reality: A Conceptual Framework
abstract: Prolonged and repetitive poor postures are often leading to various musculoskeletal dis-orders (MSDs) and significant health risks. Most of the conventional assessment methods rely on periodic evaluations and subjective observations and fall short in providing robust interventions. This paper presents a proposal of an advanced framework that integrates sensor data, machine learning (ML), and virtual reality (VR) for ergonomic risk management. The pilot study observations of the results of this framework using the Random Forest ML algorithm revealed a risk prediction accuracy of $\mathbf{9 8. 5 3 \%}$ for the musculoskeletal risk scores based on predefined posture bounds. Also, whenever an im-proper posture is detected, the system developed in this research can provide immediate feedback through the VR interface that could be useful for real-time corrective guidance so as to prevent or reduce MSDs. Such Artificial Intelligence (AI) and VR enabled interventions are very useful to enhances effective posture corrections for personnel work-ing at construction site operations.

articleTitle: From Data to Decisions: Assessing the Feasibility and Rationality of Human-in-the-Loop for AI Value Alignment
abstract: The Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) is a very important approach in machine learning, it tries to integrate human suggestions/judgements with the results from machine learning, and help it to achieve balance between efficiency and quality in data processing. It should be used in the whole process of R&D of AI, especially in the moral AI. This paper highlights the application of the HITL for AI value alignment. We analyze the technical feasibility and rationality of HITL in AI alignment, particularly in the context of Autonomous Vehicles (AVs), and discuss its potential future applications.

articleTitle: A Survey of Digital twins in Smart Farming Systems
abstract: Digital twins (DTs) have developed as a transformative technology in smart farming, facilitating real-time simulation, monitoring, and optimization of agricultural processes. This survey explores DTs’ definition and their various applications in agriculture, underscoring their ability to enhance decision-making and upsurge farm productivity. It analyses the existing surveys and explains different use cases, highlighting the projects that exemplify the DT’s practical integration in smart farming systems. The role of the Internet of Things (IoT) and machine learning (ML) in DT is also discussed for creating accurate and efficient DTs for precision agriculture. To identify gaps and areas for further research, a comparative analysis of these technologies is presented. This comprehensive survey intends to deliver understandings into the present state of DTs in smart farming, addressing challenges and providing directions for future development to improve agricultural practices.

articleTitle: Adapt2detect: Cooperative learning framework for low-lit object detection
abstract: In this work, we propose an adaptive multisensory pipeline to detect an object in the low light scenario and call it Adapt2detect. In this pipeline, we integrate LiDAR and Camera to enhance the performance of the object detection framework. We observe that in well-lit conditions, RGB sensors are the preferred choice as they provide texture and shape information, whereas, in low light conditions, we seek light-sensitive sensors like LiDAR or RADAR. In this work, we address the tradeoff of latency and accuracy. LiDAR data in well-lit conditions are expensive as RGB data suffices the objective. However, to address the challenges associated with RGB data in low-light conditions, we integrate LiDAR into the pipeline. We use scene illumination as a threshold to decide the modality object detection and the corresponding object detection framework in action. We used a variant of the YOLO and Complex-YOLO network object detection strategy in line with RGB and LiDAR data, respectively. The efficacy of integrating the LiDAR with the camera lies in reducing latency and the demand for the high compute platform.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Based Web Application Firewall for Real-Time Threat Detection
abstract: The increasing vulnerability of web applications to cyber threats necessitates the development of adaptive defense mechanisms. This paper presents the design and implementation of a Machine Learning-Based Web Application Firewall (WAF), which uses the XGBoost algorithm for real-time detection of SQL Injection (SQLi), Cross-Site Scripting (XSS), and Local File Inclusion (LFI) attacks. Unlike traditional WAFs that rely on static rule-based systems, this ML-driven solution adapts to new attack patterns by learning from web traffic data. The paper workflow encompasses data preprocessing, feature engineering, model training, and application deployment. The machine learning model was trained on a comprehensive dataset of web traffic logs, which included a diverse set of both legitimate and malicious activities. Advanced feature engineering techniques were employed to extract relevant data points from the http requests, allowing the model to capture critical details necessary for accurate threat detection. Once trained, the model was used to build the WAF. The WAF application was then placed in front of the Webserver. All incoming traffic hits the WAF and based on its analysis, it would drop the malicious traffic and allow only normal traffic to the backend Webserver.

articleTitle: Revolutionizing IPL Ticketing with NFTs
abstract: The Indian Premier League (IPL) is a widely popular cricket league hosted in India, known for its high-energy matches and star-studded players. Previously, getting IPL match tickets required long lines and physical visits to counters. With the advent of online platforms, fans can now easily purchase tickets through the official IPL website, making the ticketing process more convenient and accessible. However, the IPL ticketing system still faces significant challenges, including counterfeit tickets and scalping, which undermine the authenticity and integrity of the booking process. To address these issues, the study proposes a solution by integrating blockchain technology, particularly through NonFungible Tokens (NFTs), into the IPL ticket booking platform. The system utilizes the Ethereum blockchain to ensure the uniqueness, verifiability and transferability of IPL tickets. By leveraging smart contracts, organizers can create and manage unique NFTs for each ticket, preventing counterfeiting and ensuring a reliable record of transactions. A decentralized approach allows organizers, vendors and fans to interact directly with the blockchain, enhancing security and transparency. The system is designed to be efficient, with automated ticket issuance and transfer facilitated by smart contracts. Additionally, it promotes responsible and sustainable practices by reducing the need for physical tickets and encouraging digital event management. The following research contributes to the understanding of how blockchain and NFTs can transform the ticketing industry, fostering a more sustainable future.

articleTitle: A Neural Machine Translation Framework Utilizing Attention Mechanisms for Multilingual Date Translation
abstract: Date translation across multiple languages and formats remains an important challenge, as it is influenced by the forms of representation that vary in linguistics variations and the nuances of cultures. Although NMT has achieved major success regarding general text translations, domain-specific tasks, such as the translation task of dates across multiple languages, are relatively unexplored. We have introduced a novel approach for multilingual date translation that relies on an NMT model with an augmented attention mechanism that captures contextual dependencies by using a sequence-to-sequence architecture with a pre-attention Bi-LSTM layer. Then an attention mechanism is applied in the sequence to focus on the right parts, and the post-attention LSTM generates the translated date in the desired format. Our dataset contains various date formats, namely French, German, Spanish, Chinese, and Russian, which pose different structural and linguistic challenges. The model was trained to standardize all dates to the format of ISO 8601 (YYYY-MM-DD). We find our experiments to demonstrate a few significant areas of improvement in terms of translation accuracy and consistency, particularly format variation and language-specific date representations. Further, our work contributes toward robust multilingual NMT models, filling the gap in translating structured entities like dates and improving the understanding of applications of attention mechanisms in domain-specific tasks.

articleTitle: A Convolutional Neural Network Ensemble Model for High-Voltage Insulator Surface Image Classification
abstract: Power transmission lines use high-voltage insulators for both electrical insulation and mechanical support. In normal operating conditions, insulators are often exposed to outdoor contamination and stress from different weather conditions. These factors can lead to insulation malfunctions and power losses. Consequently, electricity grid operating companies must conduct regular check-ups and evaluations to minimize possible power outages. This paper introduces a new method that uses deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for high-voltage insulator surface image classification. Given the effective use of CNNs in computer vision, numerous pre-trained models are available for various classification tasks. Typically, researchers fine-tune these models on a specific dataset, and a single model is selected and used for the final prediction. In contrast with this “winner-take-all” approach, in this study, an ensemble of pre-trained CNNs is proposed to classify the type of pollution accumulated on the insulator surface. This focus is warranted because each pre-trained convolutional base operates as a feature extractor, and thus a combination of them as proposed in this study functions as a composite feature extractor. Our numerical results clearly show the superiority of the proposed ensemble technique over the common “winner-take-all” approach for classifying insulator surface contamination.

articleTitle: Assessing Random Forest and SARIMA Models for Wet Period Rainfall Prediction in Northern Territory, Australia
abstract: The present study investigates the simultaneous effect of climate indices on wet rainfall in the Northern Territory (NT). To achieve this, a comprehensive set of input variables was employed, including lagged indices of the Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD), El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO), and MaddenJulian Oscillation (MJO). These climatic predictors were utilized to calibrate and validate the Random Forest (RF) and Seasonal Auto-Regressive Integrated Moving Average (SARIMA) models, ensuring robust model performance and accurate rainfall forecasting. To evaluate the model’s performance, three statistical measures were used: mean absolute error (MAE), correlation coefficient (r), and root mean square error (RMSE). Among the large-scale climate factors considered, MJO, SOI, and NINO 3.4 were identified as having a significant impact on the Northern Territory’s wet period rainfall forecast. For NT forecasts at one selected station, the RF model demonstrated the most favorable outcomes. Similarly, the SARIMA model displayed a root-mean-square error (RMSE) that ranged from 8.64 mm to $\mathbf{6 0. 6 5 \mathrm {mm}}$ across the selected site. In contrast, the RF model demonstrated better performance, exhibiting an RMSE range of $\mathbf{5. 2 4} \mathbf{~ m m}$ to $\mathbf{4 9. 3 3} \mathbf{~ m m}$.

articleTitle: A High Gain Two stage Telescopic OTA Operating at 1.5V Power Supply in 180nm CMOS Technology
abstract: In Analog and Mixed-signal circuits, operational transconductance amplifiers (OTA) are crucial parts. Due to its high gain and speed, the telescopic OTA is preferred. This work aims to enhance the gain and power efficiency of Telescopic amplifiers. This paper explores design techniques to increase the OTA gain while maintaining decent power consumption by using the Cadence Virtuoso EDA tool. This paper has proposed a design to increase the open loop gain and ensure stability under a wide range of operating conditions. The proposed OTA has achieved an open loop gain of 120 dB, UGB frequency of $372.45 \mathrm{MHz}, 147.65^{\circ}$ Phase Margin and a Slew rate of $0.1 \mathrm{~V} / \mu \mathrm{s}$. The OTA consumes an overall power of $102 \mu \mathrm{~W}$ from a 1.5 V power supply.

articleTitle: Potato Leaf Disease Detection System Using the Convolutional Neural Network (ResNet)
abstract: Potato is a crucial crop on a global scale, and its productivity can be impacted by a range of diseases, including leaf diseases. Timely identification and precise diagnosis of leaf diseases can play a crucial role in preventing their rapid dissemination and mitigating potential crop damages. Over the past few years, Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in image classification tasks, such as identifying diseases in plants. Our study presents a method for effectively identifying potato leaf diseases, including early blight, late blight, and healthy leaves. We utilize a CNN model that is built on the ResNet architecture, ensuring professional and accurate results. Through the utilization of this model, our objective is to effectively classify and detect diseases in potato leaves, enabling the implementation of timely and efficient disease management strategies. The dataset contains images of healthy leaves as well as leaves that have been infected with various diseases, including early blight and late blight. The model is then utilized to categorize new images of potato leaves as either healthy or diseased. The proposed approach demonstrates a high level of accuracy, achieving 97.9% in the classification of potato leaf diseases, including early blight potato leaf disease and late blight potato leaf disease

articleTitle: Blockchain-Powered Privacy-Enhanced Design For Electric Vehicle Energy Market
abstract: Cybersecurity breaches, malware, and hacking are among the threats to which networked charging stations are susceptible. This paper suggests techniques for designing secure and authentic smart contracts for the networked electric vehicle energy market (NEVEM). The methods ensure smart contracts comply with data privacy regulations and protect sensitive user information from unauthorized access. The paper proposes the secure and authentic data structure of NEVEM. The token-based secure authentication (TSA) mechanism is presented for NEVEM to maintain data integrity.The solidity software has been used to design the secure and authentic smart contract design for electric vehicle energy trading.

articleTitle: A Vision Based Approach for Real Time Detection of Proximity Hazards around Open Wells: An Application in Open Well Safety Monitoring
abstract: Open wells are a major hazard in India’s rural and urban settings, especially for youngsters and unwary adults. The absence of safety barriers surrounding wells frequently causes mishaps, which can occasionally be fatal. This study suggests a brand-new, reasonably priced, vision-based solution that uses a CCTV camera to identify people approaching a well and sound an alarm when they get too close. The system draws boundary boxes and determines the distance between the well and the person using object detection methods to precisely detect and classify both. Accidents may be avoided if an automated alert is set off if the distance between the person and the well drops below a certain level. This method is trained using custom YOLOv8 models for well detection and a pre trained model for person detection. This paper emphasizes the system’s importance in the context of countries like India, where safety infrastructure around wells is often insufficient, and accidental falls are a common hazard.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Passive Harmonic Filter for Industrial Application Using Web-Based Automation
abstract: The design and analysis of passive harmonic filters are essential for improving power quality in industrial applications by reducing harmonic distortion. This paper focuses on automating the conventional process of designing harmonic filters. Power converters, which use Thyristors, IGBTs, MOSFETs and other fast switching devices, are commonly employed to provide controlled electric power to various electrical loads such as variable speed drives (VSDs), furnaces, solar converters, and large power supplies. However, these converters introduce harmonic and reactive power components into the AC mains due to their nonlinear nature. The objective is to minimize current distortion caused by these nonlinear loads at the Point of Common Coupling (PCC), in accordance with IEEE standards for harmonics in Electrical systems for industrial users. This is achieved using passive power filters. A web-based approach to harmonic analysis and mitigation enables the design of shunt passive power harmonic filters with both equal and unequal branch VAR configurations to be more streamlined and cost-effective.

articleTitle: Optimizing Speech Recognition for Medical Transcription: Fine-Tuning Whisper and Developing a Web Application
abstract: Utilizing automatic speech recognition in medical transcription can greatly improve healthcare professionals’ productivity. It eliminates the need for manual tasks like physician note-taking, data retrieval, and medical information searches, which can be time-consuming and divert their attention from patient care. Fine-tuning automatic speech recognition (ASR) systems for medical transcription using domain specific data is essential to enhance the performance. In this work, we fine-tuned the Whisper ASR system, which is known for its state-of-the-art speech recognition capabilities, using medical speech data. The fine-tuned model achieved a word error rate (WER) of 7.5% for medical data, demonstrating its potential for accurate transcription in clinical settings. Futher, we have developed a web application tailored for medical transcription. This application uses the robust Whisper ASR engine, renowned for its resilience to background noise. The web application offers user-friendly features such as audio recording, secure access via user-specific logins, and the seamless preservation of medical speech reports. We tested the web application with six Indian doctors by recording 362 utterances of prescriptions. The speech transcription achieved a WER of 19.4%, indicating the need for further fine-tuning for the Indian context with a larger dataset and an advanced Whisper model variant.

articleTitle: Design and Development of Smart Industrial Chemical Etching Setup for PCB Manufacturing
abstract: Printed Circuit Boards (PCBs) are important elements in practically all modern electrical appliances, and the demand for high-quality, precisely made PCBs has increased substantially with modern advances in technology. This research paper presents the design and implementation of an innovative etching system aimed at reducing wattage consumption in PCB manufacturing. The system incorporates PTC heaters, known for their self-regulating temperature control and energy efficiency. The design of the PTC heaters is detailed, and their performance is rigorously tested against that of conventional resistors. Power consumption comparisons reveal that PTC heaters consume significantly less energy, initially operating at 440 watts and decreasing further after reaching the desired temperature, whereas conventional resistors continuously consume approximately 1200 watts. Sample PCBs were manufactured using both PTC heaters and ordinary resistors, with the line widths measured and compared. The experimental results show that PTC heaters provide more consistent and precise etching due to their stable temperature maintenance, resulting in uniform PCB lines. In contrast, ordinary resistors exhibit larger temperature fluctuations, leading to variable line widths. The significance of adopting PTC heaters in the etching system and its cost comparison is discussed.

articleTitle: Enhancing Medical ASR Accuracy through the Integration of T5-Based Small Language Models and Error Correction Mechanisms
abstract: A key challenge in healthcare is the time spent on documentation, which hinders patient care. Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) technology automates this process and enhances efficiency and access to medical data. Medical ASR systems face significant challenges in accurately understanding the complexities of healthcare conversations, including various accents, dialects, and specialized terminology. Fine-tuning ASR systems with domain-specific medical speech datasets can improve performance, but the challenge of acquiring large and high-quality datasets limits accuracy. To tackle this issue, we propose an ASR output error correction method using a T5-based language model, which integrates the strengths of large language models with error correction training to improve ASR performance. The model was fine-tuned using a diverse dataset comprising synthetic text, synthetic speech, and natural speech data. Synthetic text data was generated to simulate common transcription errors, producing $\mathbf{3 0, 0 0 0}$ pairs of incorrect and correct text. For performance evaluation, synthetic speech recordings were created from 5,000 text samples using edge text-to-speech synthesizer. Additionally, natural speech data was sourced from the Medical Speech, Transcription, and Intent dataset, consisting of $\mathbf{6, 6 0 2}$ speech recordings focused on medical symptoms. Experiments were conducted to assess the model’s accuracy and Word Error Rate (WER) across these datasets. The T5-based error correction model significantly improved ASR performance, achieving an accuracy of $91.23 \%$ and a Word Error Rate (WER) of just $1.20 \%$ on synthetic text data, while also enhancing WER to $3.03 \%$ for synthetic speech and $\mathbf{3. 6 4 \%}$ for natural speech after targeted training. To evaluate the effectiveness of our models for Indian doctors and their specific context, we recorded prescription speech from six Indian doctors. The experiments on these recordings demonstrated that targeted training reduced the WER from $\mathbf{1 9. 2 5 \%}$ to $\mathbf{8. 8 9 \%}$.

articleTitle: Early Detection and Classification of Multi Crop Leaf Diseases using Custom Based CNN Model
abstract: Plant monitoring and disease diagnostics are essential to sustainable agriculture. However, plant diseases are difficult to manually monitor since they require accurate and timely diagnosis. In this paper, we propose Early Detection and Classification of Multi Crop Leaf Diseases using Custom Based Convolution Neural Network (CNN) Model. The images from standard Kaggle dataset are subjected to preprocessing which includes Resizing, Adaptive Histogram Equalization, Smoothening and Banalization. The preprocessed data is subjected to custom based CNN to obtain the high level hidden features. The proposed model is trained on data samples for different diseases with dataset types of Mango, Gauva and Chilli Leaves. This achieved average accuracy of 97.65% and precision of $\mathbf{9 6. 3 5 \%}$ for 3858 image samples. The experiment findings demonstrate that the proposed method offer a more effective way to control plant diseases.

articleTitle: Advanced Controllers for Boosting Solar Vehicle Sustainability and Efficiency
abstract: There is a huge rise in the cost of basic products and services due to the increase in crude oil prices, which also had an impact on individuals. Due to this price hike, transportation costs, inflation, and the financial burden on people are also raised. Advancements in Electric Vehicles (EVs) offer a better alternative, but their adoption has slowed down due to limited range and insufficient charging infrastructure. Utilizing renewable energy for developing Solar-powered vehicles presents a viable solution for sustainable and Eco-friendly transportation. However, low efficiency and the large size of solar panels hinder the development of such vehicles, making them less practical for extensive use. To tackle these challenges, a smart controller has been developed that can automatically switch between two batteries based on real-time voltage detection. The proposed design guarantees continuous power supply without diminishing the vehicle’s range, allowing users to drive without range anxiety while ensuring safe battery charging. The advanced controller seamlessly manages the battery power and improves the efficiency and usability of solar-powered vehicles. Automatic switching sustains battery health by preventing overcharging and extensive discharging. This auto-switch feature also prevents potential power interruptions. Additionally, the controller enables systematic monitoring of essential parameters such as voltage, current, and temperature, which are prime indicators of battery health and performance. Real-time insights on battery usage are provided for the drivers which they can use to make informed decisions about energy usage. This will certainly improve the driving experience and reduce concerns about running out of power.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of a Novel Electronic Variable Valve Actuation System Developed for a Camless Engine
abstract: Variable valve actuation (VVA) technology has the potential to enhance the energy efficiency of internal combustion engines, and its development is relevant to the global shift towards sustainable power generation. In a conventional cam-based system, valve actuation is achieved with a fixed cam profile, and the valve events are tied up with the crankshaft’s rotation and, hence, are not flexible. However, an electronic VVA system enables flexible control of the engine valve events and valve lift profile as a function of time. The present article discusses the development and performance analysis of an in-house test facility for electro-pneumatic variable valve actuation (EPVVA) system. The EPVVA system utilizes high-frequency solenoid valves. The solenoid valves control the valve lift profile. The control is achieved by the modulation of the electrical pulses sent to the solenoid valves. The engine valve events of opening and closure are independently controlled by varying the time of activation of the inlet and exit solenoid valves. The valve actuation profile of the EPVVA system is characterized with the help of a Hall-effect based position sensor. The independent control of valve lift parameters, such as peak valve lift, area under valve lift profile, and the duration of valve opening, is demonstrated with a systematic variation of control parameters as well as the timing of their initiation. The repeatability of valve actuation is assessed by conducting multi-cycle experiments. The effect of the inherent characteristics of solenoid valves, the control unit, and the working fluid on the repeatability of valve operation is quantified through statistical analysis.

articleTitle: Water Quality Assessment Using Ensemble Technique
abstract: Compromised water quality poses risks to human health which necessitates the need for accurate water quality assessment. Our paper employs ensemble machine learning to accurately classify water samples. We present a comprehensive study focusing on the application of machine learning algorithms for the classification of water samples to determine their suitability for human consumption. The soft voting technique incorporates four algorithms, namely Naive Bayes, decision tree, random forest, and ANN. To assess water quality, we calculated WQI based on 12 parameters, classifying water samples into five distinct categories: excellent, good, moderate, poor, and very poor. The ensemble model achieved an accuracy of 92.22%.

articleTitle: Low-Cost Solution for Vehicle Collision Avoidance for Smart and Safe Transportation
abstract: Moving towards smart transportation heavily depends on the state-of-the-art collision avoidance system. Intersections and inattention of drivers cause accidents. The latest vehicles have an inbuilt collision avoidance system, however, implementing it on existing vehicles is not practical as it requires hardware and sensors. Due to non-practicality and the cost incurred for the installation, existing vehicles will be far away to set up this kind of system. In this article, we propose and develop a technique based on combined Haversine and Vincenty’s formulae for collision avoidance systems to detect and warn the driver of the possibility of a collision. Our technique is incorporated into a mobile application and can be easily installed on users’ mobile. Our proposed work measures vehicle coordinates and distance between the vehicles. The prototype app warns by beeping if any other vehicle approaches around the vehicle at high speed. Further, the app data can be used to analyze the traffic and accordingly, drivers can decide on which road to reach in a minimal time. It also warns any vehicles coming from sides in intersections or lanes. Without additional cost for hardware devices, the existing vehicles can make use of this smart solution for vehicle collision avoidance.

articleTitle: Self-Training and Error Correction using Large Language Models for Medical Speech Recognition
abstract: In the healthcare sector, medical professionals must dedicate substantial time and effort to documentation, which directly impacts patient care and clinical decision-making. Automatic speech recognition (ASR) systems offer a potential solution to reduce the burden of these documentation tasks. However, conventional ASR systems often perform poorly in the medical domain due to the use of specialized terminology, as well as variations in accent and pronunciation. Fine-tuning ASR models with large amounts of medical speech data is challenging due to confidentiality concerns and limitations in recording conditions. This study explores two approaches to enhance the performance of ASR for medical speech. The first approach utilizes a self-training mechanism, where transcriptions generated by a baseline ASR model are used to train the model further. The pseudo-labels produced by the baseline model introduce greater data diversity, particularly when the model transcribes with high confidence. The second approach employs open-source large language models (LLMs) to select the most probable transcription from the fivebest hypotheses generated by the ASR model. We conducted experiments using the Whisper ASR model as the baseline and investigated the effectiveness of these two approaches. Our findings indicate that self-training reduced the word error rate (WER) by an absolute $1-2 \%$. However, the use of five-best hypothesis selection resulted in an increased WER, which we attribute to the limited medical knowledge of the open-source LLMs.

articleTitle: Citation Prediction Using LDA Topic Models
abstract: This research investigates the use of deep learning models for predicting citation counts of academic research articles, leveraging Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) scores as key features. By incorporating LDA-based topic modeling, the research explores the effectiveness of various deep learning models. The models are used to perform an analysis using the top 5 and top 10 LDA words. The results demonstrate that MLP and CNN outperform RNN models, with MLP consistently delivering the highest accuracy and lowest error rates.

articleTitle: Semantics Preserving Dimensionality Reduction of Citation Network Using Topic Models
abstract: This research focuses on constructing a more compact network from a large citation network using Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) and evaluating the efficiency and structural characteristics of the resulting network. A comparison is made between the compact LDA-derived network and the original citation network across various graph-based metrics. The results demonstrate that, despite its reduced size, the LDA-derived network retains or even improves key structural properties, enhancing efficiency while preserving critical information.

articleTitle: A Case Study on BIM-Enabled Clash Detection in a G+13 Residential Building
abstract: This study presents a cost-benefit analysis (CBA) of Building Information Modeling (BIM) for clash detection in a G+13 residential project in Mumbai, India. The Architecture, Engineering, and Construction (AEC) industry faces significant challenges, including low productivity and high costs caused by unforeseen conflicts during construction. BIM addresses these issues by creating a digital building model, enabling the early identification and resolution of design conflicts among structural, architectural, and MEP (Mechanical, Electrical, and Plumbing) systems. This research compares the long-term benefits of reduced rework, increased productivity, and enhanced project management with the initial costs of BIM implementation, such as software, infrastructure, and training expenses. A detailed case study demonstrates the substantial financial advantages of early conflict resolution, revealing that using BIM for clash detection resulted in significant cost savings of ₹365,000 on a single major conflict. Additionally, BIM clash detection minimizes material waste and CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions, promoting sustainable construction practices. The findings support the broader adoption of BIM technologies in construction, highlighting their potential to improve efficiency, reduce project delays, and deliver high-quality outcomes. This study offers valuable insights for stakeholders considering BIM implementation and contributes to the ongoing discourse regarding its role in modern construction.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Clustering-Based Analysis of the Impact of Plastic Ban on Ocean-Dependent Industries
abstract: Plastic ban in marine habitats has pushed global governments to impose stringent plastic bans. These regulations, while necessary for environmental protection, have far-reaching economic consequences, particularly for ocean-dependent companies. This study uses powerful unsupervised clustering methods to provide a detailed analysis of the economic impact of plastic restrictions on various businesses. Using K-means with Manhattan and Minkowski distance metrics, as well as spectral clustering, we hope to find hidden patterns in the economic disturbances produced by these prohibitions. The employment of multiple distance metrics in K-means enables robust evaluation across diverse data distributions, whereas spectral clustering captures complicated non-linear correlations. Our findings show that different sectors of the marine economy face varying degrees of financial stress, providing insight into how these companies respond to regulatory changes. This study contributes to our current understanding of the socioeconomic effects of environmental regulations by providing data-driven insights to help improve decision-making and policy formulation for sustainable ocean management. The findings of this study further highlight the necessity for sector-specific interventions, as the economic impact is not uniformly distributed across all industries. For instance, fisheries and tourism-related businesses are particularly vulnerable, while shipping and offshore energy sectors show more resilience to the regulations. Additionally, the study reveals regional disparities in how businesses are affected, with smaller island nations bearing a disproportionate burden due to their reliance on ocean-based industries. By incorporating unsupervised clustering, this analysis provides a nuanced view of these impacts, highlighting the importance of tailored regulatory frameworks. Policymakers can leverage these findings to balance environmental sustainability with economic vitality in oceandependent regions.

articleTitle: Digital Twin-based Flight Dynamics Simulation
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) systems face significant challenges during critical flight phases, such as post-liftoff stabilization and mid-flight disturbance response. This paper presents a Virtual Reality (VR) based simulation and control system integrated with a digital twin to enhance the understanding of UAV dynamics. The system uses real-time data from the UAV’s Onboard Computer (OBC) to create a dynamic 3D environment where users can interact with flight parameters such as position, rotational dynamics, and vibration amplitude. This approach enables the analysis of UAV performance and stability under changing conditions by allowing real-time adjustments. This immersive system supports research, training, and operational optimization of aerospace systems.

articleTitle: Beyond Training Data: Zero-Shot Mathematical Problem Solving with Large Language Models
abstract: This study investigates the potential of Large Language Models (LLMs) for mathematical problem solving using a zero-shot multi-path self-consistency technique combined with programmatic solution verification. We create Python code that is evaluated by a majority vote by providing multiple reasoning pathways using differences in temperature and top-k values, as well as improving inquiry comprehension through phrasing. When applied to the GSM8K and MATH datasets, this approach achieved $\mathbf{45 \%}$ accuracy on GSM8K and $\mathbf{14.57 \%}$ on MATH with the Granite 8B code model. These findings show that even in the absence of task-specific training data, LLMs can greatly enhance their performance by breaking down complicated tasks and employing a consistent multipath technique.

articleTitle: A Cost-Benefit Analysis of Employee Layoffs versus Workforce Management Strategies: Assessing Financial Impacts and Organizational Profitability
abstract: Companies frequently use layoffs to minimize expenses during economic instability or organizational change, despite the possible detrimental impact on staff morale and business culture, so organizations consistently confront significant workforce management issues, particularly when deciding between employee layoffs and alternative measures like flexible staffing or retraining programs. This study investigates the financial consequences of these decisions, emphasizing how they influence profitability in organizational performance. The study leverages sophisticated algorithmic learning techniques those are Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machines (SVM), and Random Forests were chosen for their ability to forecast financial consequences, categorize workforce tactics, and provide accurate insights into short and long-term organizational performance to examine and compare the effects of employee layoffs to other workforce management measures. Logistic Regression calculates the likelihood of various financial consequences based on labor actions. SVM aids in categorizing and predicting the effectiveness of multiple tactics by determining the best decision boundaries between them. Random Forests improve forecast accuracy by merging several decision trees, providing a strong analysis of financial implications and operational precision. By providing a thorough examination of how layoffs and alternative methods influence financial performance and operational accuracy, the findings give practical insights that may help organizations implement more successful and sustainable managerial procedures. This, in turn, contributes to increased profitability and operational efficiency by aligning staff management decisions with overall organizational goals.

articleTitle: The Irreducibility of Consciousness in Human Intelligence: Implications for AI, Legal Accountability, and the Human-in-the-Loop Approach
abstract: This paper proposes a framework that adapts irreducible consciousness to govern human-AI co-design, positioning consciousness as central to intelligence. Drawing insights from quantum mechanics, infant cognitive development, the limbic system, and the philosophical hard problem of consciousness, we explore the implications of consciousness for human-AI codesigns. We address legal complexities, such as interpreting mens rea (guilty mind) in AI-mediated actions, especially as AI, neurotechnology, and brain-computer interfaces (BCI) increasingly blur distinctions between human volition and AI behaviours. Our model identifies principles of mind and core mental fac-tors-consciousness, feeling, perception, volition, contact, and attention-and aligns them with brain data using BCI. Through the Markov Decision Process (MDP) framework, we integrate BCI brain data with behavioural and contextual information to strengthen human oversight and reinforce the human-in-the-loop paradigm in human-AI co-design. This framework suggests a need for evolved ethical and legal accountability approaches to address the complex realities of human-AI collaboration.

articleTitle: LLMs as Debate Partners: Utilizing Genetic Algorithms and Adversarial Search for Adaptive Arguments
abstract: This paper introduces DebateBrawl, an innovative AI-powered debate platform that integrates Large Language Models (LLMs), Genetic Algorithms (GA), and Adversarial Search (AS) to create an adaptive and engaging debating experience. DebateBrawl addresses the limitations of traditional LLMs in strategic planning by incorporating evolutionary optimization and game-theoretic techniques. The system demonstrates remarkable performance in generating coherent, contextually relevant arguments while adapting its strategy in real-time. Experimental results involving 23 debates show balanced outcomes between AI and human participants, with the AI system achieving an average score of ${2. 7 2}$ compared to the human average of ${2. 6 7}$ out of 10. User feedback indicates significant improvements in debating skills and a highly satisfactory learning experience, with 85% of users reporting improved debating abilities and ${7 8 \%}$ finding the AI opponent appropriately challenging. The system’s ability to maintain high factual accuracy (92% compared to ${7 8 \%}$ in human-only debates) while generating diverse arguments addresses critical concerns in AI-assisted discourse. DebateBrawl not only serves as an effective educational tool but also contributes to the broader goal of improving public discourse through AI-assisted argumentation. The paper discusses the ethical implications of AI in persuasive contexts and outlines the measures implemented to ensure responsible development and deployment of the system, including robust fact-checking mechanisms and transparency in decision-making processes.

articleTitle: Harnessing the Power of Industrial Artificial Intelligence for Optimization of Manufacturing
abstract: Industrial AI primarily focusses on the application of AI technologies rather than development of human or human-like systems. Manufacturing is the largest sector in the global economy with a major share in Gross Domestic Product (GDP). Therefore, Industrial AI in manufacturing can have a significant impact on improving the productivity, thereby increasing the overall efficiency of this sector. This paper brings out the applications, pros and cons of integration of AI in manufacturing industry functions such as design, material management, production planning, quality assurance, supply chain management, etc. The challenges and opportunities in adopting Industrial AI in small scale industries is also showcased. Overall, integration of Industrial AI into manufacturing leverages industries to be competitive in global markets.

articleTitle: Cassava Leaf Disease Detection using Seresnext-50 with Attention
abstract: Cassava, a crucial staple crop faces persistent threats from various diseases, significantly undermining food security and economic stability in the region. Traditional methods of disease detection rely heavily on manual inspection by agricultural experts, presenting challenges of scalability and accessibility for smallholder farmers. In response, this research endeavors to introduce a data-driven solution by utilizing deep learning techniques for automated classification of cassava leaves. In this research a novel methodology is proposed for automatic detection of the cassava leaves into five classes (four diseased and one healthy) using deep learning techniques. The proposed methodology incorporates transfer learning strategy to train SEResNext50 32x4d model with self-attention mechanism. The experiments are performed over cassava leaf disease dataset. The results confirm the efficiency of the approach introduced, showcasing significant accuracy of 0.9647 for “Cassava Mosaic Disease” and an overall accuracy of 0.8988 in image classification leading to efficiently utilize the method in detecting diseased leaves through computer-aided-diagnostic systems.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Inference based Pedestrian and Cyclist Tracking in a Compressed Video
abstract: In recent times, the artificial intelligence (AI) based technologies are pervading the various human activities, for instance, smart manufacturing plants and autonomous driving vehicles (ADVs) on roads. With the advent of Industry 4.0, it is of common occurrence that human workers and autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) coexist and collaborate in the various tasks of smart manufacturing plants. The humans could be either walking or riding a bicycle in case of large area plants such as paper manufacturing industries. Thus, the industrial safety and traffic safety become cause of primary concern in the usage of AMRs and ADVs, respectively, which entails the need for equipping these intelligent devices with computer vision for detecting the humans, who are either walking or cycling, in their path of mobility, and thus avoid their collision. The integration of such detection systems is crucial for maintaining safe interactions between humans and machines. In the present study, a novel methodology based on fuzzy inferencing is designed for video analytics in the compressed domain, aimed at real-time detection and tracking of pedestrians and cyclists, by utilizing motion vectors (MV) and Transformer Prediction Heads-You Only Look Once version five (TPH-YOLOv5). The video compression formats MPEG-4 and H. 264 are considered. The proposed method can be adapted to any compression format and video camera settings without any prior setup. In the literature, many algorithms for tracking of pedestrians and cyclists in a compressed domain video are experimented, but these have some limitations such as (i) a fixed interval for keyframe occurrence, (ii) utilization of only $\mathbf{P}$ frames, and (iii) setup for only a single video codec. The proposed method is designed to address these limitations by employing keyframe intervals of variable length, utilizing P and B frames, and setting up two codecs MPEG-4 and H.264. Further the event box prediction in video frames is done by fuzzy inferencing. The benchmark video datasets, namely, Tsinghua-TDC, SCD, and KITTI datasets are considered for the experimentation. The ablation study has been carried out by choosing different variants of proposed method arising due to different video codecs, fuzzy representations, video datasets.

articleTitle: Overcoming DNSSEC Islands of Security: A TLS and IP-Based Certificate Solution
abstract: The Domain Name System (DNS) serves as the backbone of the Internet, primarily translating domain names to IP addresses. Over time, various enhancements have been introduced to strengthen the integrity of DNS. Among these, DNSSEC stands out as a leading cryptographic solution. It protects against attacks (such as DNS spoofing) by establishing a chain of trust throughout the DNS nameserver hierarchy. However, DNSSEC’s effectiveness is compromised when there is a break in this chain, resulting in “Islands of Security”, where domains can authenticate locally but not across hierarchical levels, leading to a loss of trust and validation between them. Leading approaches to addressing these issues were centralized, with a single authority maintaining some kind of bulletin board. This approach requires significantly more infrastructure and places excessive trust in the entity responsible for managing it properly. In this paper, we propose a decentralized approach to addressing gaps in DNSSEC’s chain of trust, commonly referred to as “Islands of Security”. We leverage TLS and IP-based certificates to enable end-to-end authentication between hierarchical levels, eliminating the need for uniform DNSSEC deployment across every level of the DNS hierarchy. This approach enhances the overall integrity of DNSSEC, while reducing dependence on registrars for maintaining signature records to verify the child nameserver’s authenticity. By offering a more flexible and efficient solution, our method strengthens DNS security and streamlines deployment across diverse environments.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of U-Net, PSPNet, AND FPNet: Deep Learning Techniques for Image Segmentation
abstract: With applications ranging from environmental monitoring to autonomous driving and medical imaging, image segmentation is a crucial problem in computer vision. It involves partitioning images into meaningful regions to assist in object detection and classification. Traditional methods struggle to capture complex features, while deep learning techniques excel by learning hierarchical representations, leading to greater accuracy and efficiency. This paper provides a detailed comparison of three deep learning-based segmentation models: U-Net, PSPNet, and FPN (Feature Pyramid Network), focusing on how each one tackles pixel-wise classification in unique ways. U-Net’s encoder-decoder architecture with skip connections is well-suited for tasks that require precise boundary delineation, while PSPNet’s pyramid pooling captures global context at multiple scales, and FPN constructs feature pyramids to handle multi-scale object detection and segmentation. We assess the strengths and weaknesses of these models in terms of architecture, computational efficiency, and performance on benchmark datasets. Metrics such as accuracy, Intersection-over-Union (IoU), and computational time reveal that U-Net is especially effective for tasks requiring precise localization, whereas PSPNet and FPN excel at managing complex, multi-scale features. This analysis highlights the importance of choosing the right model for specific segmentation challenges and explores ideas for future improvements, such as combining model features for better performance. Practical applications in fields like autonomous systems and medical imaging are also discussed.

articleTitle: Next-Gen Electric Vehicle Battery Optimization: Enhancing RUL Prediction with Regression-Based Algorithms
abstract: Batteries have become the central component of energy storage frameworks, playing a crucial role in supplying power to various devices and technologies. Among this, rechargeable electrochemical storage or batteries made with lithium-ion have a high density of energy while offering a lightweight structure and relatively low self-discharge rates. They have emerged as an essential component of modern battery backup systems, especially in electric vehicles (EVs). However, concerns related over their limited lifespan and continuous, subtle decline within the battery capacity, and long-term reliability pose barriers to their widespread adoption. This research work focuses on enhancing the estimation of RUL (Remaining Useful Life) through the utilization of data-driven techniques. These techniques are growing increasingly and are essential for battery management in vital industrial sectors such as electric vehicles and solar energy storage. Although traditional machine learning models are effective in certain circumstances, they frequently lack the robustness and reliability required for accurate RUL prediction. To address these challenges, we are utilizing Random Forest(RF), LightGBM (LGBM), and a hybrid of these models to boost prediction accuracy and reliability. The hybrid model performs more effectively in reducing errors and improving predictive accuracy, eliminating the limitations of individual algorithms, which was tested on datasets that involve lithium-ion batteries. In accordance with our research, this approach provides a more reliable way of estimating the health of batteries, contributing to safer battery management systems whilst being effective.

articleTitle: Improving Emotion Detection in Audio Using Deep Learning Algorithms
abstract: Emotion analysis in audio-based systems has become an important research topic in recent years, as understanding speech-based human emotions has various practical applications, such as improving human-computer interaction, enhancing emotional communication, and aiding in mental health support via audio-based chatbot systems. Emotion detection using audio faces limitations such as emotion ambiguity in audio files, limitations in feature representations, and generalization concerning varying accents and dialects. This paper showcases a comparative analysis of various deep-learning algorithms for emotion analysis via audio signals. Spectrogram-based feature representation and audio-based feature representations have also been implemented and compared. To evaluate the effectiveness of the approach, the authors conducted experiments on the publicly available SAVEE dataset. Among the implemented algorithms, CNN (with spectrograms) and RNN (with MFCC) have showcased an improved accuracy of 61%.

articleTitle: Explainable AI and Big Data Analytics for Data Security Risk and Privacy Issues in the Financial Industry
abstract: This paper is a comprehensive review of the current literature on the importance of data security in the financial industry when working with Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) and Big Data Analytics. Collaborative initiatives in the financial industry have significantly propelled the rapid evolution of e-Commerce with the help of data and have spurred the implementation of advanced technology such as data analysis and explainable AI (XAI) that can provide human-understandable explanations on the reason for providing a good level of transparency and traceability for decisions made [1]. This growth raises concerns regarding secure data processing and preserving privacy within the database used for data mining and cost-effective big data analytics including structured, unstructured, and semi-structured data crucial for decision making along with maintaining the integrity and accuracy of stored data. The reliance on explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) for data analytics has raised critical concerns, highlighting the need for comprehensive strategies to state the importance of maintaining data privacy and security. Ensuring the protection of sensitive information while harnessing the power of analytics for decision making becomes a critical challenge that demands immediate attention. Explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) is the most important technology used in the financial sector for decision-making on applications that require explaining the reasons that made the algorithm model come with the outcome, as customers have the right to know on what basis the result of their application was evaluated. Although much research has been conducted on the technological function of XAI research on how to process these data securely and safely remains very limited [2]. To address these necessities, this research aims to provide insights into the best ways to conduct data analytics in a privacy-conscious world and to ensure that data analytics can be conducted with the help of XAI, which will help maximize the efficiency of automated data processing and provides the result with an explanation for the reason for the result. This research paper will contribute to the existing literature on data analytics with AI and provides analysis for the financial industry to improve its data analytics capabilities, providing insights and guidance in optimizing big data analytics within the financial sector addressing cost-effectiveness, privacy concerns, and efficiency in data model selection for enhanced decision-making and operational performance. The unique insights or advancements the paper offers to the existing body of knowledge are a thorough analysis of current explainable AI techniques and their applications in addressing data security, risk, and privacy challenges specific to the financial sector, a new framework that integrates explainable AI with big data analytics to enhance data security and privacy in financial institutions, introduction of an innovative risk assessment model that leverages explainable AI to identify and mitigate potential security threats in financial data systems, a new innovative risk assessment model that leverages explainable AI to identify and mitigate potential security threats in financial data systems, presenting a new novel privacy-preserving techniques that utilize explainable AI to protect sensitive financial information while maintaining data utility, identification of key areas for future research, highlighting potential advancements in explainable AI that could further improve data security and privacy in the financial industry for future research directions.

articleTitle: KannadaGPT: Tuning Language Model for Kannada Text Generation
abstract: This study describes an approach for optimizing a pretrained language model for Kannada text production. We leverage the GPT-2 architecture, which was first trained on a large Kannada corpus, to build a strong language model capable of comprehending and producing coherent Kannada text. The model is further refined using a dataset including pairs of prompts and their accompanying completions, allowing it to provide contextually appropriate and linguistically precise replies. The process is divided into two stages: pre-training to establish a generic language understanding, and strategy fine-tuning to improve model output quality. Due to computing resource constraints, the model was trained across fewer epochs on limited datasets; nevertheless, the suggested technique provides a foundation that may be extended and refined to increase performance. The evaluation of the fine-tuned model shows considerable gains in generating meaningful and contextually suitable Kannada text, indicating its potential applicability in a variety of Kannada-specific Natural Language Processing (NLP) tasks. Attention maps visualization is also examined to highlight which words or tokens in a phrase have the most influence on predicting the following word in transformer-based models.

articleTitle: Landslide Vulnerability Assessment Using Frequency Ratio Method: A Case Study of Irshalwadi Village, Raigad, Maharashtra
abstract: A very heavy 265 mm rainfall in a day on 19<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> July 2023 at Irshalwadi, Maharashtra, had triggered a disastrous landslide at the geologically unstable village of the Western Ghats. The landslide had brought upon huge devastation, and loss of human lives in the region. Our research tries to figure out all the direct and indirect contributing factors and understand the correlations among them that led to this cataclysmic event. This research uses frequency ratio (FR) based technique for Landslide Susceptibility Mapping (LSM) of the Irshalwadi area. The proposed approach meticulously integrates diverse variables such as rainfall pattern in the area, slope of the land, aspect, curvature, distance to drainage, LULC, & geomorphology to define the landslide prone zones within the area and to precisely assess the landslide vulnerability of the area. By analyzing the results, we could clarify the efficacy in capturing the nuances of landslide dynamics by FR technique. Validation of the LSM model of Irshalwadi area was conducted using the Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) curve method. It produced a degree of validation accuracy which is significant enough in delineating landslide susceptibility for the given region. Our findings offer a pathway towards encouraging disaster preparedness and fostering resilience in similar landslide-prone areas of Western Ghats and India.

articleTitle: Image Denoising using Traditional and Attention Based Techniques: A Survey
abstract: In this paper, the goal is to explore models for reducing noise in images while preserving important details like textures and edges. The paper covers various methods used for image denoising, ranging from traditional approaches like Block Matching and 3D Filtering (BM3D) and Principal Component Analysis (PCA) to more advanced methods using deep learning. The focus is on how newer models like Autoencoders, Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), and have improved denoising by learning patterns in noisy images. The paper also highlights cuttingedge models like Vision Transformers (ViTs) and Denoising Convolutional Neural Networks (DnCNNs), which use innovative ways to analyze and clean images by treating images as sequences or patches, helping achieve better results. Advancement in deep learning has enhanced the ability of the denoising the images while maintaining crucial details. Models like ViTs and DnCNNs have become the most widely used solutions in order to balance noise reduction.

Author Keywords: DnCNNs and deep learning with attention

articleTitle: Smart Traffic Management: A Deep Learning Approach for Congestion Reduction using YOLOV8 & RandomForest
abstract: Traffic management has become a tedious task for policemen to carry out manually. According to the publication produced by Bureau of Police Research & Department in 2017, India has just about 72,000 traffic cops to manage almost $20,000,000$ vehicles. As the ratio is insanely high and unmanageable, traffic congestion has increased ever since. Hence, we proposed a smart traffic management system which will particularly tackle this problem using cutting edgetechnology. By analyzing the oncoming traffic, our model predicts the required time for particular vehicles to pass and adjusts the signal timings accordingly. By combining models from deep learning and machine learning we, propose a cheap, efficient system that addresses these problems by a combination of YOLOv8 & Random Forest Regression to generate results. These results consist of annotated images and timings for signals which are calculated from the vehicle count.

articleTitle: Low volume production layout optimization — An intelligent enabler based model
abstract: The manufacturing industry is witnessing an increase in demand for low volume individualized composite products. However, integrating this process intensive composite manufacturing into the traditional materials based production line requires an adaptive and dynamic factory layout planning. Isolated simulation models cannot address the complexities involved in seamless integration of distinct products to existing production lines. Hence, this paper proposes a transformative technology enabled Digital Twin (DT) integrated system that leverages data, based on appropriate level of abstraction to simplify the system. The model leverages a combination of Discrete Event Simulation (DES) and Agent Based Modeling (ABM) to accurately represent a carbon fiber production facility. The proposed model analyzed both independent and correlated variables and identified key enablers that influence layout planning decisions. The integrated model revealed that the Double Diaphragm Preforming workstation experienced $\sim 65 \%$ idle time. The correlated variables led to locating targeted iterations through Pearson’s correlation coefficient analysis and identified strong interdependencies of 0.9967 between press tool and trimming workstations. This novel technique provided insights on machine interactions and optimize complex systems using hybrid simulation and an immersive environment. The proposed framework established flexibility through targeted parameter adjustments and improved responsiveness towards the dynamic production landscape.

articleTitle: Implementation and Comparison of Path Planning Algorithms for Autonomous Navigation
abstract: In autonomous navigation, efficient path planning is critical for ensuring robust and reliable performance in dynamic environments. This paper presents a comparative study of two widely-used path planning algorithms: Dynamic Window Approach (DWA) and $A^{*}$ algorithm, among other leading algorithms, implemented using Robot Operating System (ROS) on the TurtleBot3 platform. The DWA algorithm focuses on real-time obstacle avoidance and local path optimization, while $A^{*}$ provides a global path solution based on heuristic search. Through a series of experiments in simulated and real-world scenarios, the effectiveness of the algorithms in terms of computational efficiency, path optimality, and adaptability to dynamic obstacles has been evaluated. The findings highlight the strengths and limitations of each approach, providing valuable insights for the development of autonomous systems in various applications. This study aims to contribute to the ongoing efforts in enhancing the autonomy and reliability of mobile robots. Notable enhancements in terms of travel distance, time and overall path have been recorded, and the combined approach shows significant improvement in Path Distance (approximately 3.53%), Travel Time (approximately $\mathbf{6. 6 2 \%}$), and Travel Distance (approximately $\mathbf{3 0. 1 7 \%}$).

articleTitle: Spoken Languages Identification for Indian Languages in Real World Condition
abstract: This work uses deep learning and advanced audio features to detect Indian spoken languages. Using pre-trained models such as wav2vec, data2vec, and ccc-wav2vec, we retrieved the feature representations of audio. Spoken language identification models were trained independently on each feature representation. To achieve this, an utterance-level embedding called u-vector with WSSL (within-sample similarity loss) is trained along with a simple DNN (Deep Neural Network) classifier on these features. In this paper, 12 Indian-spoken languages (including English) are considered and trained for only 10 hours of speech data from each language. The results show that using these feature representations and utterance-level embedding, a simple DNN can efficiently identify different Indian languages.

articleTitle: Navigating Uncertainty: Gold Price Forecasting with Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks in Volatile Markets
abstract: This study presents a comprehensive evaluation of multiple forecasting models for predicting gold prices, including traditional MLP-based models like LSTM, N-HiTS, and TSMixer, as well as the Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (KAN), within the KAN-MLP Hybrid Multivariate Market Forecasting Framework. This framework integrates diverse data sources, including gold prices, external financial indices like the U.S. Dollar Index and silver prices, and sentiment analysis derived from textual data. After preprocessing, these features are fed into the models to assess their performance in handling multivariate time series data during periods of market volatility. Evaluation metrics-MAPE, RMSE, MAE, MSE, and MASE-were employed to assess the models’ accuracy and computational efficiency. Results indicate that KAN consistently outperforms other models, achieving the lowest forecasting errors across various feature combinations. For example, with only gold and the U.S. Dollar Index (USDI) as features, KAN achieved a MAPE of $\mathbf{4. 1 \%}(\pm 1.3)$ and RMSE of 4.0 (±1.2), highlighting its accuracy and stability. KAN also proved exceptionally efficient, with training times ranging from 0.5 to 0.8 seconds, far lower than N -HiTS and TSMixer, which required up to 63.6 seconds for training on more complex feature sets. In contrast, LSTM, N-HiTS, and TSMixer showed more variability in performance and required longer training times. Traditional ARIMA models performed poorly, with a MAPE as high as 68.2%, underscoring their limitations in handling complex, non-linear data. Despite KAN’s success, limitations exist, such as the exclusion of external macroeconomic and geopolitical factors and the need for further hyperparameter tuning. Overall, the KANMLP Hybrid Framework provides a powerful, flexible solution for financial forecasting, offering significant improvements in accuracy and computational efficiency compared to traditional methods.

articleTitle: Revolutionising Digital Construction: A Conceptual Framework from the Integration of DTs and BC for Enhanced Assets Management to Share Knowledge
abstract: This study presents a conceptual framework that integrates Digital Twins (DTs) and Blockchain (BC) technology for enhanced asset management in the construction industry, mainly focusing on permit certification. The proposed framework effectively addresses critical challenges such as data security and transparency by utilising DTs to create accurate digital representations of physical assets and employing BC to ensure secure and transparent data management. The framework also integrates Knowledge Management Systems (KMS) to enable effective knowledge sharing of the permit certification. This research not only highlights the benefits and challenges of the proposed integration but also points to the exciting potential for future research on how Artificial Intelligence (AI) could further revolutionise and optimise these integrated systems.

articleTitle: Heart Health Insights: Analysing Data and Visualising Predictive Factors for Cardiovascular Disease
abstract: Cardiovascular Diseases (CVDs) are a leading cause of mortality worldwide, posing a significant public health challenge. This study aims to contribute to the existing research on CVD prediction by exploring the application of data analysis and visualization techniques. The researchers employed a range of machine learning algorithms, such as decision trees, support vector machines, random forest, and logistic regression, to analyze a comprehensive dataset of $\mathbf{1, 1 9 0}$ observations with 11 independent variables and the presence or absence of heart disease. The study focused on identifying the most significant factors contributing to the risk of heart disease using Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and evaluating the accuracy of different machine learning models in predicting the likelihood of CVDs. The findings offer important insights into how data analytics and visualization can be applied to detect and prevent cardiovascular diseases early on.

articleTitle: Enhanced COVID-19 Detection Using Attention-Augmented ResNet with Inception Modules and Regularization Techniques
abstract: This research proposes a novel deep-learning model for accurate COVID-19 detection from lung CT scans. By enhancing the ResNet-50 architecture with Convolutional Block Attention Modules (CBAM) and Inception modules, the model effectively captures multi-scale features and refines attention, improving diagnostic accuracy. A comprehensive preprocessing pipeline, including data augmentation, ensures the model’s generalizability across diverse datasets. The model was validated using using publicly available balanced datasets and a 5 -fold cross-validation strategy, demonstrating superior performance compared to traditional models like DenseNet and EfficientNet. The proposed approach achieved a highest notable ${9 9. 8 1 \%}$ accuracy in COVID-19 classification, outperforming existing methods. These results highlight the model’s potential as a reliable diagnostic tool in clinical settings, particularly for early detection and treatment planning. Future work will focus on expanding the dataset and exploring ensemble methods to further improve generalizability.

articleTitle: Comparison of Fair and FIFO Schedulers on Cloud Cluster of Apache Spark
abstract: Apache Spark has become a key platform for processing large-scale datasets, particularly in predictive analytics and machine learning tasks, leveraging its in-memory capabilities and scalability. Efficient job scheduling is critical to optimising the performance of Spark clusters, minimising resource consumption, and reducing execution times.In this study, we compare the performance of two widely used Spark schedulers, FIFO and Fair, on Spark MLlib tasks for two algorithms, Parallel Frequent Pattern Growth (PFP-Growth) and Random Forest, focusing on their execution times and resource utilisation across varying cloud cluster sizes. To perform this analysis, we set up Spark clusters with different configurations, ranging from 1 to 30 worker nodes, in a controlled environment.Our experiments reveal that the Fair scheduler consistently outperforms the FIFO scheduler, particularly as the cloud cluster scales from small to moderate sizes. The Fair scheduler’s ability to dynamically allocate resources and manage concurrent jobs more efficiently leads to reduced execution times and better overall cloud cluster utilisation, making it a preferable choice for multi-job Spark workloads. These findings offer insights to optimise Spark deployments in real-world applications, where resource management and task scheduling play crucial roles in performance and cost efficiency.

articleTitle: Digital Transformation for Sustainable and Resilient Infrastructure: Current Progress and Future Potential
abstract: Integrating smart materials and technological advancements in construction is pivotal for sustainable development. The construction industry continues to evolve with advancements in materials and technologies to enhance efficiency, sustainability, and resilience. This review article delves into recent advancements in digital construction, focusing on 3D concrete printing technology and its transformative impact on the construction industry. It explores key technological innovations and quantitative research studies on bringing resilience and improved 3D printing systems. The study examines digital transformation, sustainability and resilience and presents insightful case studies, offering a comprehensive view of current progress and future potential in this field. For this study, bibliometric and scientometric analysis methods were used. Articles were selected from peer-reviewed journals indexed in Web of Science and Scopus. These innovations can redefine construction practices, enhancing durability and efficiency in a rapidly evolving industry. As a result, structures are becoming more adaptive and long-lasting, capable of withstanding environmental challenges and reducing the carbon footprint. The synergy between advanced sustainability and digital transformation paves the way for smarter, more efficient construction processes, ultimately contributing to a more resilient built environment for future generations.

articleTitle: AI-Powered Weed Control: Image Processing and Robotics in Agriculture
abstract: This paper reviews the recent advancements in AI-driven weed management, focusing on image processing techniques and robotic approaches. With the integration of artificial intelligence, the agricultural sector can achieve precise weed detection and control, leading to improved crop yields and sustainable farming practices. This review explores various methodologies, challenges, and future directions in this field.

articleTitle: A Multi-Objective Feature Selection Framework for Breast Cancer Data Using Evolutionary Methods
abstract: Feature selection is a critical component in the development of predictive models for medical data, where high-dimensionality and the need for interpretability pose significant challenges.
