This research proposes a novel multi-objective feature selection framework that integrates domain expert knowledge with data-driven insights from machine learning models, specifically using random forest feature selection. By assigning weights to features based on expert ratings and random forest importance scores, we employ our proposed algorithm to optimize feature subsets. The proposed method addresses both the dimensionality reduction and accuracy improvement objectives, ensuring the selected features are not only predictive but also clinically relevant. Empirical validation on various medical datasets demonstrates the effectiveness of this approach in enhancing classification performance while maintaining model interpretability. This research bridges the gap between domain expertise and computational feature selection, offering a robust solution for complex medical data analysis.

articleTitle: Exploring the Use of Spatial Pyramid Pooling for CNN-based QbE-STD Systems
abstract: Query-by-Example (QbE) based spoken term detection in audio search matches an audio query with reference utterances to identify relevant ones. The traditional CNN-based QbE-STD method uses size-normalized images, classified as relevant or non-relevant, derived from matching matrices calculated between the query and reference utterances using an appropriate metric. In this study, we explore improving the CNN-based QbE-STD process by integrating a Spatial Pyramid Pooling Layer before the Fully Connected Layers in the CNN. This allows handling of input images of various sizes without the need for resizing. We evaluate its effectiveness using both single-size and multi-size input training methods, compared to the traditional size-normalized input training. This method is expected to be more efficient as the CNN learns to process the original representations of the matching matrices, rather than the potentially distorted and incomplete normalized versions resulting from resizing or other preprocessing steps. The effectiveness of our proposed method is tested using the TIMIT dataset.

articleTitle: A Multi-Functional Web Tool for Comprehensive Threat Detection Through IP Address Analysis
abstract: In recent years, the advances in digitalisation have also adversely contributed to the significant rise in cybercrimes. Hence, building the threat intelligence to shield against rising cybercrimes has become a fundamental requisite. Internet Protocol (IP) addresses play a crucial role in the threat intelligence and prevention of cyber crimes. However, we have noticed the lack of one-stop, free, and open-source tools that can analyse IP addresses. Hence, this work introduces a comprehensive web tool for advanced IP address characterisation. Our tool offers a wide range of features, including geolocation, blocklist check, VPN detection, proxy detection, bot detection, Tor detection, port scan, and accurate domain statistics that include the details about the name servers and registrar information. In addition, our tool calculates a confidence score based on a weighted sum of publicly accessible online results from different reliable sources to give users a dependable measure of accuracy. Further, to improve performance, our tool also incorporates a local database for caching the results, to enable fast content retrieval with minimal external Web API calls. Our tool supports domain names and IPv4 addresses, making it a multi-functional and powerful IP analyser tool for threat intelligence. Our tool is available at www.ipanalyzer.in

articleTitle: Efficient Deployment of Quantized Vision Transformers: A Survey
abstract: Vision Transformers have demonstrated significant potential across various tasks in the evolving landscape of computer vision. However, deploying these models on resource-constrained devices remains a challenge, particularly in optimizing the trade-offs between accuracy, latency, and model size. This survey investigates four prominent Vision Transformer models CrossViT, DualVit, ResT, and LocalViT and two advanced quantization techniques, AdaLog and Bi-ViT. It also explores the unique architectural challenges of each ViT model and evaluates the effectiveness of combining these models with post-training quantization techniques. Specific challenges addressed include the asymmetric distribution of activations post-GELU and the unbalanced nature of softmax outputs. Through detailed comparative analysis, considering top- 1 and top- 5 accuracy, latency, and model size, this study identifies DualViT combined with AdaLog as the most optimal solution. This combination maintained $\mathbf{8 3. 1 2 \%}$ Top-1 accuracy, with a reduction of model size by 83.4%, dropping from 94.04 MB to $\mathbf{1 5. 6} \mathrm{MB}$. This approach demonstrated the best performance across multiple metrics, offering insights into efficient deployment strategies for ViTs in real-world applications.

articleTitle: A Screening Framework for Data Quality Estimation in Manufacturing
abstract: In the context of Industry 4.0, Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL) offer transformative potential for manufacturing, including defect reduction and process optimization. However, challenges such as noise, class imbalance, and limited high-quality labeled data often undermine the effectiveness of ML/DL models in industrial settings. It is often not clear whether these challenges will prevent an effective model from being formed. These challenges highlight the need for robust data quality assessment methodologies to guide the data preprocessing and model training processes. This paper introduces the Tao Index, a novel metric designed to comprehensively assess the quality of industrial data by integrating both local metrics, such as distance, density, and intrinsic dimension, and global measures, including Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD) and Kolmogorov-Smirnov (K-S) distance. The Tao Index can serve as a predictor of model performance, and by identifying low separability early, it helps avoid costly investments in low-performance models and guides data cleanup, collection, and trend analysis efforts. Extensive experiments on benchmark and real-world datasets demonstrate that the Tao Index offers a realistic assessment of data quality, with deviations from empirical expectations less than $10 \%$ in all separable benchmark and real datasets, outperforming existing metrics in multiple scenarios. Moreover, the Tao Index shows strong generalization power across different industrial domains with consistent performance on different industrial datasets.

articleTitle: A Review of Acoustic Signal-based Detection of Damage in Railway Tracks
abstract: Regular inspection of railway tracks is critical for providing safety and efficiency in railway transportation systems to minimize accidents, maintenance costs and improve reliability by early detection. In this paper, a systematic review for damage detection in railway tracks using Acoustic Signals (sound generated at the wheel and track interaction point) during the movement of the train is presented. Distributed Acoustic Sensing (DAS) is a valuable method for quick, long-distance monitoring of railway maintenance and technological development and crucial for accident avoidance. In regions prone to frequent train accidents, free automation of inspection processes is essential to prevent disasters and to provide safe and reliable operation of train vehicles. A wide range of Structural Health Monitoring (SHM) systems sensor data is noisy, making Machine Learning (ML) algorithms paramount for detecting abnormal railroad conditions among many others and achieving higher accuracy in maintenance and inspection. Several advanced signal processing techniques are used to recognize crack or misalignment patterns by employing Fourier transform and wavelet analysis. Further, the signals are classified through machine learning algorithms to classify between normal and damaged conditions, presenting a non-invasive, real-time and economic monitoring system that validates the system’s capability to detect several types of damage and could enhance rail infrastructure safety. Integration of these acoustic sensing with a set of trains in a predictive analytics framework makes the study of the field a scalable tool for efficient railway management.

articleTitle: Smart Engineering Informatics and Digital Solutions for Efficient Produced Water Treatment with Nanocomposite Membranes
abstract: In sectors like oil and gas, where it is necessary to treat water polluted with metals, salts, and hydrocarbons effectively, produced water treatment poses serious environmental problems. This research investigates how smart engineering informatics and nanocomposite membranes can be combined to improve produced water treatment efficiency. While digital techniques, including as real-time monitoring and AI-driven optimization, are applied to lower operational costs and improve treatment sustainability, advanced materials, such as polybenzimidazole (PBI), graphene oxide (GO), and reduced graphene oxide (rGO), are used to improve membrane performance. Comparing the research to standard approaches, it shows enhanced pollutant removal, energy savings, and membrane longevity. The results provide a technique to scale up the application of digitalized nano-composite water treatment technologies

articleTitle: Swarm vs Evolutionary Algorithms for Path Optimization on Lunar Surfaces: A Metaheuristic Approach
abstract: Path optimization is a critical challenge in autonomous lunar exploration, where efficient traversal of rugged terrain is vital for mission success. Compared to other celestial bodies, the lunar environment presents unique challenges such as extreme temperature variations, high radiation levels, and a lack of atmosphere, making it a critical focus for autonomous exploration. Additionally, unlike other distant planets, the Moon’s proximity to Earth and its potential for future human missions makes it a priority for path optimization research. Traditional machine learning algorithms often fall short in this domain due to their dependency on large datasets and tendency to over-fit. They are incompetent when dealing with dynamically changing environments like lunar terrain. These algorithms also struggle with the unpredictability of rugged terrains, which demand real-time adaptability and robustness—qualities that machine learning techniques often lack. In this study, we address these limitations by employing meta-heuristic algorithms, specifically Differential Evolution (DE), Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), and Ant Colony Optimization (ACO). Lunar terrains, characterized by craters, sharp slopes, and high-cost traversal areas, require algorithms like DE, which uses mutation and recombination for exploration, PSO for efficient search through particle velocity updates, and ACO for intelligent path selection based on pheromone trails. Applying these methods to a simulated lunar dataset with varying terrain costs, we compare their effectiveness in path-finding, emphasizing their ability to minimize traversal costs while navigating complex, uncertain environments more reliably than traditional approaches.

articleTitle: BIM and IoT Sensors Data Integration for Improving the Efficienty of Concrete Curing Process
abstract: Determining the early-age compression strength of concrete is an integral part of many construction projects. This paper investigates the feasibility of a method to monitor temperatures related to concrete curing using IoT and BIM technology. The research includes analysis of temperature data and whether it is practical to rely on sensor-based data gathering to determine the compressive strength of concrete. To achieve this, an arrangement of temperature sensors was fixed to a series of concrete core samples as they cured, and the temperature data feed was linked to a BIM platform. It was found that the integration between IoT and BIM technologies was functional and significantly contributed towards more cost effective, efficient and accurate practices. This is particularly important if predictions on future compressive strength can be made using current sensor information. Further testing would be required to determine the heat of hydration and accurately predict the compressive strength.

articleTitle: Statistical Modeling of Spine MRI: GMM and AGMM-Based Segmentation for Lumbar Angle Classification
abstract: The precise provision of medical services with the goal of maintaining and improving health via prevention, diagnosis, treatment, and rehabilitation is referred to as healthcare. Spinal problems greatly impair mobility and quality of life, thus diagnosing and treating them is essential. The lumbar spine is composed of five vertebrae. (L1 to L5) are essential for maintaining body weight and safeguarding the spinal cord and nerves. Accurate diagnostic techniques are crucial for the prevention and treatment of diseases including spinal stenosis and degenerative disc degeneration. In order to diagnose spinal problems, medical imaging, MRI in particular, is frequently utilized. Segmenting the lumbar spine from MRI scans is a crucial part of this process, which entails locating important anatomical features such the vertebrae, inter vertebral discs, and spinal canal. The constraints of manual operations have made automated segmentation methods-especially machine learning techniques-essential because they offer higher levels of efficiency and precision. This study focuses on AGMM (Adaptive Gaussian Mixture Model) and GMM (Gaussian Mixture Model) statistical modeling techniques for lumbar spine segmentation. These models offer flexible approaches for handling the unpredictability of MRI data. In order to evaluate the Lumbar Lordotic Angle (LLA) or Lumbosacral Angle (LSA), which is essential for identifying aberrant curvatures such scoliosis and lordosis, the study intends to categorize segmented lumbar spine areas. Regarding robustness, computing efficiency, and segmentation accuracy against noise and artifacts, the efficacy of GMM and AGMM are evaluated. The results could improve the clinical use of MRI in spinal healthcare by offering new perspectives on how to best use machine learning algorithms for better imaging results.

articleTitle: A Novel RoPE-Enhanced Informer Approach for Accurate Remaining Useful Life Prediction of Lithium-Ion Batteries
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries are integral to various systems, including electric vehicles and warehouses, where estimating their operational lifespan is critical. This lifespan, known as Remaining Useful Life (RUL), helps in optimizing performance and maintenance. Accurate RUL prediction helps avoid unexpected breakdowns and lowers maintenance costs, making these systems more reliable. This paper introduces a novel approach using a Rotary Positional Embedding (RoPE) Enhanced Informer model to address challenges in long-term time series forecasting for RUL prediction. By integrating RoPE into the Informer, the model efficiently preserves positional information and leverages sparse attention mechanisms to reduce computational complexity, enabling it to handle longer sequences with minimal memory usage. The proposed model was tested on benchmark datasets, where it outperformed peer level approaches in terms of Mean Absolute Error and Root Mean Squared Error. The results show a significant reduction in validation errors, indicating the model’s superior generalization ability and its robustness against overfitting. This approach offers a scalable solution suitable for real-time predictive maintenance, particularly in resource-constrained environments. The combination of advanced positional encoding with the Informer architecture demonstrates the potential for this method to enhance battery management and improve the accuracy of RUL prediction across various industrial applications.

articleTitle: Detection and Identification of Welding Defects Through Deep Learning Models
abstract: The use of welding components has grown significantly across a wide range of industries recently, making their quality and reliability an essential component of product design and manufacturing. Determining the flaws including gaps, misalignment, cracks, spatter, and other imperfections in weld components is a laborious task that calls for expert workers and time-consuming manual examinations. The proposed algorithm entails using a collection of pictures of weld components with and without flaws to train a deep learning architecture. The model is trained through the application of transfer learning methods, and is optimized to achieve higher accuracy and lower false positives. The proposed algorithm’s efficiency is evaluated with respect to its speed and accuracy. The objective is to evaluate the accuracy of a few of the deep learning models leading to combining manual tasks with artificial intelligence approaches. The inference is that You Look Only Once-version 5 (YOLOv5) architecture provides precision scores relating to dispersion, gaps, and misalignment of $\mathbf{2 0 \%}$, $\mathbf{2 5 \%}$, and $\mathbf{5 0 \%}$, with a mean average precision (mAP) of $50 \%-60 \%$ and YOLO $\mathbf{v} 8$ architecture provides precision scores of $39 \%$, $35 \%$ and $55 \%$ with a mAP of $55 \%-65 \%$ respectively. Considerable increase in accuracy together with time and resource savings is achieved by incorporating artificial intelligence for automatic detection and classification of welded components, which results in decrease of human intervention for quality control.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison of Machine Learning Classifiers for FPGA-Accelerated Surface Defect Detection
abstract: This research paper presents the results obtained for surface defect detection on metal clamps and classifying defective and defect-free metal clamps using object detection on the PYNQZ2 FPGA development board. The object detection algorithms used in this experiment are the Haar cascade classifier and the Local Binary Pattern (LBP) classifier. The results are compared while performing the classification using the processing system alone. Also, while using the FPGA hardware accelerator, the performance of both classifiers is compared. The experiment aims to assess the impact of hardware acceleration, specifically by including programmable logic, on processing time and resource utilization. The results demonstrate the advantages of employing hardware acceleration through the programmable logic in object detection. The system achieves remarkable reductions in CPU and wall time, significantly improving processing speed while maintaining detection accuracy.

articleTitle: Hierarchical Attention Mechanism for Domain-invariant Spoken Language Identification via Inter-domain Alignment and Intra-domain Language Discrimination
abstract: Modern methods for spoken language identification (LID) have demonstrated promising results when trained on large datasets. However, their effectiveness is considerably impacted by the discrepancies between the training and testing distributions. Unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) addresses the domain discrepancies by aligning feature distributions across source and target domains without using labeled target data, thereby ensuring the model performs consistently across both domains. This alignment, however, may come at the cost of reduced model discriminability. To enhance performance under domainmismatched conditions, a LID system should learn domaininvariant representations of speech while maintaining language discriminability at every level, from initial segment-level representations to final utterance-level representations. To address this issue, in this paper, we propose a hierarchical attention network that simultaneously enhances model domain invariance through inter-domain alignment and improves model’s language discriminability using intra-domain contrastive discrimination. The performance on the target domain shows that the proposed method exceeds the effectiveness of the top-performing existing approaches.

articleTitle: VocalEyes: Enhancing Environmental Perception for the Visually Impaired through Vision-Language Models and Distance-Aware Object Detection
abstract: With an increasing demand for assistive technologies that promote the independence and mobility of visually impaired people, this study suggests an innovative real-time system that gives audio descriptions of a user’s surroundings to improve situational awareness. The system acquires live video input and processes it with a quantized and fine-tuned Florence-2 big model, adjusted to 4-bit accuracy for efficient operation on low-power edge devices such as the NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano. By transforming the video signal into frames with a 5 -frame latency, the model provides rapid and contextually pertinent descriptions of objects, pedestrians, and barriers, together with their estimated distances. The system employs Parler TTS Mini, a lightweight and adaptable Text-to-Speech (TTS) solution, for efficient audio feedback. It accommodates 34 distinct speaker types and enables customization of speech tone, pace, and style to suit user requirements. This study examines the quantization and fine-tuning techniques utilized to modify the Florence-2 model for this application, illustrating how the integration of a compact model architecture with a versatile TTS component improves real-time performance and user experience. The proposed system is assessed based on its accuracy, efficiency, and usefulness, providing a viable option to aid vision-impaired users in navigating their surroundings securely and successfully.

articleTitle: Advancements in Face Sketch Recognition: Techniques and Challenges
abstract: Face is a key contributor for criminal identification in law enforcement agencies. Forensic Sketches act as a link between suspect identification and eyewitness descriptions, which is essential to criminal investigations. The sketch artist in forensic investigations typically develop their sketches based on spoken information given by an eyewitness regarding the suspect. These drawings are created by the artist either by hand (Forensic sketches) or with the aid of a tool (Composite sketches). There is dissonance in the facial features of a sketch since the eyewitness’s memory is used to describe the features of the face. Traditional approaches relied heavily on manual comparison, which is time-consuming and prone to human error. Advances in the field of Machine Learning and Computer Vision have led to considerable improvements in the accuracy and efficiency of matching forensic/composite sketching with digital photos. Recently, A range of sketch-to-photograph retrieval strategies have been presented by various researchers, nevertheless they often ignore the uncertainty of facial characteristics for questionable faces. This corresponding study gives a thorough analysis of the approaches which are currently available for matching suspect face sketches with digital photos. The review focuses on the dataset, conventional techniques and its classification and demonstrates how suspect face retrieval methods have changed over time. Additionally, it provides a summary of the overall effectiveness of excellent state-of-the-art methods.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Deep Learning Model for Early Detection of Epileptic Seizures
abstract: Epilepsy, a condition affecting millions worldwide is characterized by recurring seizures. EEG (Electroencephalography) offers a direct assessment of the brain’s electrical activity. This non-invasive measurement technique, with its high temporal resolution, enables the detection of specific seizure patterns. Early and precise prediction of seizures is crucial in preventing consequences like status epilepticus and sudden unexpected death in epilepsy (SUDEP). The objective of this study is to develop an advanced seizure detection algorithm with high accuracy. In our proposed model band analysis and feature extraction are done using Short Time Fourier Transform (STFT) and these features are passed to a hybrid model of CNN2D (network with 2D input) and Bidirectional Long Short Term Memory (BiLSTM) model. This model is validated across various patient profiles. Results indicate that the CNN2D+BiLSTM model outperforms other existing models in terms of prediction accuracy and speed. Furthermore, adaptive learning mechanisms enhance detection capabilities over time. This study makes use of the CHB MIT Scalp EEG Database and the Siena Scalp EEG Database, which contain EEG recordings from 500 individuals. Key performance measures include: OVLP: Overlap ratio signifying intersection between true and predicted events. EPOCH: Analyzing the alignment of labels and predictions in a time frame, for each EEG channel. ROC Curve: Illustrates the balance between sensitivity and specificity.

articleTitle: Balancing Reward and Safety: An Analysis of Reinforcement Learning Agents
abstract: This work presents a comparative analysis of Trust Region Policy Optimization (TRPO), Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), and Constrained Policy Optimization (CPO) algorithms for robotic path planning, using a panda robotic arm in the PyBullet simulation environment. The work aims to identify the most suitable reinforcement learning (RL) agent by evaluating each algorithm based on learning efficiency, safety adherence, and effectiveness in policy development. Safety metrics such as constraint violations, recovery time, and risk of unsafe actions were measured to assess safety adherence in various scenarios. Through rigorous simulation-based testing, this work explores key factors such as convergence rates, sample efficiency, safety performance, and generalization capabilities. Interestingly, while some agents demonstrate strong performance during training, they may struggle in application scenarios, revealing the potential disconnect between training success and practical application. This work also sheds light on the unique manifestation of overfitting in RL, where agents tend to rely heavily on learned actions, becoming vulnerable to minor environmental changes. This underscores the importance of balancing exploration and exploitation to avoid local optima and foster robust generalization. By offering a detailed comparison of these algorithms, the findings provide insights into the strengths and limitations of each, offering recommendations for selecting appropriate RL techniques for applications on robotic path planning, with a focus on safety and robustness in dynamic environments.

articleTitle: An Integrated Platform for Lie Detection and Plagiarism analysis in Interviews
abstract: This paper discusses an advanced interview platform that integrates AI-driven technologies for interview integrity and authenticity. It is possible to record video-based interviews with built-in functionalities including identifying lying, plagiarism analysis, and stress evaluation. Video recording is carried out simultaneously while concurrently recording the audio; transcripts are also generated. The transcripts are consequently passed through the Winston AI plagiarism checker to search for signs of internet usage during the interview. Facial analysis is used to measure stress and detect deception in real-time. The tool generates a comprehensive integrity report and provides an innovative tool to carry out safe and reliable interviews.

articleTitle: Integrating Advanced Machine Learning, Sensor Fusion, and Control Systems to Enhance Autonomous Vehicle Safety and Performance
abstract: Self-driving vehicles are right now one of the most progressive elements in the contemporary automotive industry, they may bring significant improvements for traffic safety, traffic intensity, and emission levels. However, reaching the necessary level of operational reliability for masse implementation implies surmounting issues with real-time occupancy decision making, precise localization, and accurate object identification. This paper presents a systematic approach to these problems using Machine Learning algorithms, Sensor Fusion, and Control Systems. Namely, the framework assesses CNNs and RNNs in core AV functions based on detection, classification, and trajectory prediction capabilities. In CNN evaluation arises with a classification of $94 \%$ and $F 1$ score was $\mathbf{9 4 \%}$ In the similar classification, RNN has a minimal error of $0 \%$ with overall accuracy of $\mathbf{9 1 \%}$ and precision of $\mathbf{9 0 \%}$. For increasing the accomplishment of localization and perception, different sensor fusion techniques were discussed and based on the conclusion that the EKF offered improved performance; the proposed approach achieved accurate localization up to 0.20 meters and an object detection of percent 94. Based on these results, an improved cost function was formulated, and an MPC solution was thus applied. This approach provides a tracking error which was reduced to 0.10 meters, and it has excellent performance compared to the basic PID and LQR control in similar circumstances. In doing so, this work lays down a strong foundation for further research on AV technology and the relevance of human expertise on future $A V$ systems safety and efficiency.

articleTitle: Advancements in Digitalization and Automation in the Construction Industry towards Sustainable Infrastructure: Present and Future Perspectives
abstract: The construction industry is facing challenges in data management, quality, safety and decision-making due to its complexity and fragmented nature. Engineering informatics provides essential tools and methods to streamline the construction processes and enables data-driven decisions, enhances project quality and efficiency, supports sustainability development, and reduces project costs by integrating intelligent data processing into the construction lifecycle. The objective of this review article is to provide a comprehensive overview of the state-of-the-art in digitalization and automation in the construction industry, encompassing the various engineering informatics employed in the construction industry such as additive manufacturing in construction, building information modelling, internet of things, digital twin in construction, artificial intelligence, and machine learning. The present study utilized a systematic review methodology to thoroughly assess literature on digitalization and automation in the construction industry towards sustainability. Based on the review, it can be concluded that compared to conventional methods, additive manufacturing in construction offers high resource efficiency, reduces waste, requires minimal labor, and enables the creation of complex designs. The review led to identify the potential of building information modelling and Internet of Things technology which enhances transparency, efficiency, and security in construction projects, enabling real-time monitoring, tracking, and data integrity. Digital twin technology offers transformative potential for construction, enabling enhanced planning, design efficiency, improve structural analysis, mix properties, and sustainability. Additionally, key findings shows that AI and ML enhances data security, integrity, safety and transparency, addressing critical risks across the construction lifecycle. This paper is significant for both academic and industrialists, focusing on sustainability involving advancements in digitalization and automation.

articleTitle: Real-Time MRI Synthesis from Text Using a Two-Stage Pipeline for Pronunciation Training
abstract: Providing visual or animated information on how to position and move the tongue and other speech articulators is beneficial for children with hearing impairments to improve their pronunciation. However, since these articulatory movements occur inside the mouth, they are not visible. Real-time MRI of the midsagittal plane of the mouth can be used to extract this information. However, acquiring MRI data for every word is both time-consuming and impractical. This work proposes a method to synthesize MRI sequences for a given text. The approach involves a two-stage pipeline. In the first stage, text-to-speech synthesis is performed to replicate the speaker’s voice characteristics. In the second stage, the synthesized speech is mapped to an MRI sequence using a speech-MRI mapping model trained on the speaker recordings. The synthesized speech and corresponding rtMRI sequences are then integrated to generate a synchronized rtMRI video, providing a simultaneous representation of both articulatory movements and acoustic output. A key advantage of the proposed method is that it eliminates the requirement for phoneme-to-MRI frame alignment during the training of phoneme-to-MRI mapping models, a process that is frequently error-prone when relying on forced-alignment techniques. The Tortoise-TTS system is employed for speech synthesis from the text, ensuring that the generated speech matches the target speaker’s voice characteristics. A bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory network is trained to map speech to the corresponding MRI image sequence. To evaluate the synthesized MRI sequences, both objective measures, such as Frechet Inception Distance, and subjective evaluations are utilized. The mean FID scores ranged from 94.23 to 135.28, comparable to those obtained using other forced alignment-based methods. Subjective evaluations on a 1-to-5 scale yielded an average score of 3.5. The results demonstrate that the generated MRI sequences are realistic and closely resemble natural recordings, with performance metrics indicating a satisfactory level of accuracy and quality.

articleTitle: Knowledge Distillation Using Deep Learning Techniques: A Survey
abstract: In Deep Neural Networks (DNNs), optimization is necessary for adjusting model parameters to reduce the loss function, which directly affects the model’s performance. Effective optimization techniques reduce prediction errors and help models generalize new data better. One method discussed in this document is Knowledge Distillation (KD), where a “student” model which is smaller is trained using the knowledge imparted by a larger, more complex “teacher” model. KD was first focused on DNN compression for resource-efficient deep learning, but it has now been extended to privileged learning, adversarial defense, and noisy data learning. Some of the most important techniques in distillation include online distillation, involving training Teacher and student models operate together. for end-to-end optimization; offline distillation, where the teacher model guides the student model based on lessons learned; and self-distillation where a model learns from its previous iterations. Advanced methods such as adversarial distillation, which combines adversarial procedures to improve information transmission, and lifetime distillation, in which historical data educates current models to preserve stability and avoid performance decline. Applications span across domains like Computer vision (CV), Natural Language Processing (NLP) and speech recognition, demonstrating the versatility and importance of KD in deploying powerful models in resource-constrained environments.

articleTitle: Text-to-Image Synthesis for Heritage Monuments Using Generative Adversarial Networks: A Survey
abstract: India’s architectural heritage, including iconic structures like the temples of the Vijayanagara Empire, faces significant preservation challenges from factors such as wars, neglect, and environmental degradation. Artificial Intelligence (AI) offers innovative solutions for heritage conservation, providing advanced tools for documenting, analyzing, and digitally restoring these cultural assets. Among AI technologies, Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) stand out for their ability to reconstruct and visualize heritage sites from textual descriptions, enabling digital restoration and preservation. GANs can realistically recreate lost or damaged elements, offering a virtual glimpse into the past that supports both education and awareness. By providing immersive experiences through virtual tours and digital reconstructions, GANs can help raise global awareness about India’s rich architectural legacy, while also engaging local communities in the importance of preservation. This technology allows for interactive exploration, empowering conservationists to make informed decisions that balance historical accuracy with modern conservation needs. Ultimately, GANs play a crucial role in safeguarding India’s architectural heritage for future generations, fostering deeper public understanding and appreciation both locally and globally.

articleTitle: The Future of Patient Care: Revolutionizing Treatment Plans through Deep Learning and Precision Medicine
abstract: The evolution of patient care is increasingly influenced by precision medicine, which seeks to customize medical treatments based on the unique characteristics of each individual. However, the integration of advanced technologies, particularly deep learning, poses significant challenges and opportunities in this domain. This study investigates the application of deep learning algorithms in crafting precision medicine strategies, addressing critical research problems such as the analysis of intricate datasets that encompass genomic, proteomic, and clinical information. We propose a robust framework that leverages convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and recurrent neural networks (RNNs) to effectively identify biomarkers and forecast patient-specific responses to various therapies, with a focus on diseases like cancer and cardiovascular conditions. Our results indicate that deep learning models markedly improve the accuracy of disease prediction and the personalization of treatment plans compared to conventional approaches. Furthermore, we examine the hurdles related to data variability, the interpretability of models, and ethical implications tied to the implementation of these technologies in clinical practice. Through detailed case studies, we highlight how deep learning can transform patient care by facilitating more precise and individualized treatment strategies. This research emphasizes the necessity for interdisciplinary collaboration in advancing precision medicine and outlines potential pathways for integrating artificial intelligence into healthcare systems.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of Driver Drowsiness Detection and Fatigue Analysis using CNN, GAN, and Hardware Models
abstract: Driver drowsiness and fatigue are significant road safety risks, leading to numerous accidents globally. This research presents a comparative analysis of Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) approaches for real-time driver drowsiness detection. We developed both hardware models, integrating sensors with vehicle dashboards, and software models using deep learning architectures for feature extraction and analysis. Extensive datasets were used to train and evaluate the models under varying conditions. Results demonstrate both approaches’ effectiveness, with nuanced differences in detection accuracy, sensitivity, and computational efficiency. Insights into the strengths and limitations of each method guide the selection of suitable techniques for real-world applications, with recommendations for future enhancements including model optimization, ADAS integration, and deployment in autonomous vehicles.

articleTitle: Robot Rover Intelligence Offloading Through a 5G Network
abstract: Network Slicing (NS) and Software Defined Networking (SDN) are network virtualization technologies that optimize the utilization of infrastructure and resource allocation to make the Beyond 5G (B5G) network more flexible. The software-defined control in mobile networks, especially in the Radio Access Network (RAN) — enables a broader range of use cases and new services, as well as easier future evolution via programmability. At the same time, developing a software-defined RAN (SD-RAN) is difficult due to the unique nature of the wireless resources to be managed and the strict timing constraints associated with certain key RAN control operations like resource scheduling.This paper explores the scheduling mechanisms that cover both the downlink and the uplink to slash the latency for UltraReliable Low Latency Communications (URLLC) slices even in the situation where the radio resources are being shared among multiple users with different scheduling algorithms such as round-robin, fair proportion, and maximum throughput. In addition, this paper demonstrates the effect of static as well as dynamic resource allocation on the key performance indicators (i.e., latency and throughput) of individual users under various network loads and network configurations.

articleTitle: Smart manufacturing and management system for efficiency enhancement
abstract: Smart manufacturing has exponentially grown in an industrial context, globally resulting in a prime national strategy. Interconnecting and converging various non-flexible technologies within an industrial context is the main barrier to its adaptation and implementation. The challenge of interconnecting multi-characterized manufacturing systems with cyber and providing streamlined real-time interfacing is a fundamental issue. This research focuses on the development of Smart Manufacturing and Management System (SMMS) framework to address the manufacturing challenges in cable manufacturing, by acquiring manufacturing characteristics and converging to cyber systems for smart analytics interfacing physical machines, virtual systems, managers, and shop floor operators. The proposed SMMS has been implemented in cable manufacturing and it has shown the potential to reduce the manufacturing time to $\mathbf{\sim 2 0 \%}$ and cost to AUD $\mathbf{1 8 0, 0 0 0}$ per annum. to the traditional process. So, it’s clear that SMMS implementation will enhance manufacturing efficiency, quality with faster decision capability, reduced wastage and cost. Additionally, given the challenges faced by manufacturing, this system adopted will reduce the fierce global manufacturing competitiveness, especially for low-volume personalized products.

articleTitle: Stylizing Images Using Generative Adversarial Networks
abstract: This paper, addresses the very real challenge of changing photographic images of reality into corresponding cartoon images by working with advanced GANs. Working on the foundation established for CartoonGAN, it was trained over an extensive dataset that exceeded more than 45,000 images derived from the works of Makoto Shinkai at Studio Ghibli, regarded as among the greatest in his sector. Apart from CartoonGAN, StyleGAN3 and CycleGAN are considered as benchmarks for results. These models are assessed based on the retention of content, sharpness of the edges, viewership engagement, different variations in the output, quality of art, and uniformity of style. Qualitative survey is conducted for 150 participants and asked to rank the images generated by the model for all the metrics mentioned. The model performs well within the scope of the purposes without the necessity of an extensive exhaustive search, as this qualitative survey distinctly gauges the success of the proposed model against all the existing techniques, indicating the ability of the model and the remnant areas that require improvement. The results demonstrate that the approach possesses better content retention and style consistency than other methods since it produces plausible and high-quality cartoon-to-photo transformations. For future work, the model will be further fine-tuned and trained on the increased dataset’s size for enhancement of robustness and generalizing the performance altogether.

articleTitle: Transfer-learning based multi-class areca nut image classification under uncontrolled lighting on a conveyor system for automated sorting
abstract: Areca nut is an important cash crop with high cultural and economic significance to the Indian demography. The level of ripeness can be visually assessed based on the color and is an important deciding factor for the market value of the crop and subsequent post-harvest processing such as drying, de-husking, etc. The quality assessment and segregation task, when carried out by manual labor is subjective, inconsistent, and prone to be tedious with inadvertent errors and loss in the desired efficiency. The advent of computer vision (CV)--based segregation techniques along with deep learning (DL) neural network (NN) models can augment the manual efforts in the segregation process in the agri-food sector. A fast, low-cost conveyor-based system that performs multi-class classification of areca nuts based on color and a preliminary image dataset of areca nut images captured using the same is presented here, along with explorations of some pre-trained neural network models. A feeding mechanism, a conveyor system, and a sorter system were designed and fabricated using traditional machining and 3D printing processes. A dataset of RGB images of harvested areca nuts comprising around 1600 images of areca nuts on the conveyor belt under uncontrolled lighting conditions was generated to simulate the challenging industry-relevant sorting scenarios. Transfer learning using pretrained models like Inception-V3, Resnet50 and others was utilized to implement the classification. Using contour detection and Hough circle-based automated cropping, and manual cropping, four different versions of the original dataset created were used along with two variations in dataset split and two learning rates. Inception-V3 exhibited the highest testing accuracy of 91.98% for the 80-10-10 train-cross-validation-test percentage split with a 0.0001 learning rate, with Resnet50, Inception-Resnetv2 and VGG16 exhibiting 68.52%, 90.74% and 88.27% respectively. All methods of image cropping, including manual, adversely affected all models’ classification accuracy and performance metrics, possibly owing to loss of information during cropping or file conversion operations. VGG16 was found to be more sensitive to the cropping of RoI in the image than other models. Thus, for transfer learning, the dataset preprocessing needs careful consideration.

articleTitle: AI Driven LLM integrated diffusion models for Image Enhancement- A Survey
abstract: Text-to-image generation has emerged as a prominent research problem in computer vision and natural language processing, resulting from recent progress in generative models and LLMs. This paper reviews the latest research on Text-to-image generation models integrated with Large Language Models (LLMs). The paper focuses on the analysis of six LLM integrated models namely DiffusionGPT, LLM Grounded Diffusion Model, IN-STRUCTCV, ECLIPSE, Self-Correcting LLM-Controlled Diffusion Models and SUR adapter. Each model is evaluated based on its architecture, methodology and results. Our analysis identifies the advantages and disadvantages of different models and provides recommendations for further research directions. At the end of this paper is a summary of the current advancements in the field and suggestions for future study possibilities.

articleTitle: Hand Pose Detection Using YOLOv8-pose
abstract: Hand detection and pose estimation are prominent problems in computer vision. They have applications in augmented and virtual reality, human-robot interaction, and gesture recognition which can be incorporated into controlling various interfaces, such as those used in assistive technology. The hand detection problem involves three sub-problems, i.e. hand localisation, hand classification, and pose estimation. Different hand detection methods approach this problem in multiple stages. However, there is a scope to train an end-to-end network that addresses these three problems at once. In this paper, we contribute to hand detection, classification, and pose estimation by first modifying the FreiHAND dataset to ensure both left and right hand images, along with their annotations, are present for training. Then, we train the YOLOv8-pose networks from nano to extra-large sizes to perform a comparative study of the performance of each network. Further, we perform quantitative and qualitative analysis on three public hand datasets that shows the strengths and limitations of YOLOv8-pose networks. Our experiments on training YOLOv8-pose networks from nano to extra-large sizes showed that the mean average precision score increases with the network size. We also conclude that the ratio of hand size to the image size in training affects the confidence score and classification during inference detection.

articleTitle: SPP-DeepFilterNet: Integrating Speech Presence Probability for Speech Enhancement using Deep Learning
abstract: Speech enhancement, critical for applications like voice communication, hearing aids, and speech recognition, has greatly advanced with the integration of deep learning and filtering approaches. Hybrid methods combining these techniques have shown exceptional promise in mitigating complex noise sources and significantly improving speech quality. However, the current state-of-the-art deep filter model for speech enhancement faces challenges in achieving optimal performance, particularly in complex acoustic environments with diverse noise sources and variable signal conditions. To address these limitations, this research investigates methods for enhancing the deep filter model’s capabilities by integrating additional signal features. Specifically, the research objective is to enhance the performance of the existing DeepFilterNet2 model through the integration of the speech presence probability (SPP) feature as an additional feature, alongside the existing ERB (equivalent rectangular bandwidth) and complex features. Termed as SPP-DeepFilterNet, our proposed model leverages a speech model comprising both periodic and stochastic components. The model’s first stage operates in the ERB domain, enhancing the speech envelope, while the second stage utilizes deep filtering to enhance the periodic component. We hypothesize that the inclusion of SPP synergistically enhances the model’s ability to improve speech quality and intelligibility, ensuring adaptability and robustness across diverse real-world scenarios. Evaluation using objective measures and spectrogram analysis demonstrates improved performance, particularly in unseen noisy conditions, validating the efficacy of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Transforming Tourism Loyalty Programmes through Private Blockchain
abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of a private blockchain-based loyalty programme tailored for the tourism and hospitality industry to address challenges in traditional loyalty programmes such as limited interoperability, high administrative costs, fraud susceptibility, and data privacy concerns. By leveraging private blockchain technology, the proposed system enhances trust, transparency, and operational efficiency among administrators, merchants, and customers. A comprehensive PESTLE and SWOT analysis was conducted to assess external and internal factors influencing the adoption of blockchain technology, identifying key success factors and potential risks. A use-case diagram illustrates the system’s interactions, highlighting the roles of administrators managing the blockchain and loyalty system, merchants integrating services and managing rewards, and customers earning and redeeming loyalty points. A prototype was developed using the Meta61 Blockchain platform to demonstrate practical applicability, featuring secure transaction recording, smart contracts for loyalty point management, and enhanced data privacy. While acknowledging limitations such as initial integration costs, complexity for SMEs, and dependency on a central authority, the paper suggests future work including exploring hybrid blockchain models, integrating decentralised identity management technologies, and developing user education strategies to increase adoption. In conclusion, the implementation of a private blockchain-based loyalty programme has the potential to transform the tourism and hospitality industry by improving multi-party trust, operational efficiency, and customer engagement, positioning blockchain technology as a transformative force addressing inherent limitations of traditional loyalty programmes and fostering enhanced collaboration among stakeholders.

articleTitle: Condition diagnosis of a screw extrusion process through energy consumption curve monitoring
abstract: Traditionally, energy monitoring of processes was motivated by environmental concerns, disconnected from the actual process performance and reliability. However, energy and performance are intertwined, meaning a degraded system condition can cause power consumption changes. This paper presents an approach to condition monitoring, fault detection and diagnosis based on the calibration of energy operational curves, the relationship between a system’s power consumption and its operational performance. It differs from approaches that solely rely on the energy profiles over time, and instead extracts information from the coefficients of the relationship obtained by measuring the power consumption of the system against a sweep across one of its inputs. The approach was applied to a screw polymer extrusion machine, on which temperature faults and contaminated material were introduced. The proposed approach was able to detect a barrel temperature fault of a $\mathbf{1 0 \%}$ deviation as well as a contamination level of $15 \%$, all simply by studying the energy operational curve shifts. The approach offers a simpler option of instrumentation to diagnose equipment operational faults.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Analysis Of Complex Clotting Data For Precise Blood Disorder Detection Using Advanced Machine Learning Techniques
abstract: In medical diagnostics, the reliable detection of blood disorders is critical for improving patient care and ensuring optimal treatment outcomes. Blood clotting is a vital physiological process that prevents excessive bleeding by forming clots. However, disorders related to abnormal clotting can severely impact health, making precise diagnosis essential for effective treatment Conventional diagnostic methods often fail to manage the complex nature of blood clotting data, leading to challenges in precision and accuracy. This gap highlights the need for more advanced tools to enhance the reliability of disorder detection. This study introduces an innovative classification model designed to accurately assess and analyze complex blood clotting data for the precise detection of blood disorders. The research employs sophisticated machine learning strategies, including Random Forest, Decision Tree Classifier, and Rotational Forest, to build a robust classification model. The methodology integrates meticulous feature selection, comprehensive data preprocessing, and advanced classification algorithms. Rigorous training and validation protocols are implemented to ensure dependable performance. The model’s performance is evaluated using key metrics such as precision, recall, accuracy, and F1 score. The results demonstrate that the model significantly improves the reliability of disorder detection and aids in developing personalized treatment plans for patients. By incorporating cutting-edge machine learning techniques. This research significantly advances diagnostic methodologies for detecting blood disorders. It establishes new benchmarks in diagnosing hematological conditions, paving the way for more precise and individualized patient care solutions.

articleTitle: Leveraging Boosting Algorithms for Accurate Battery Life Prediction in Autonomous Robots
abstract: Autonomous robots are self-operating systems equipped with advanced algorithms and sensors, enabling them to navigate, perform tasks, and make decisions independently. Precise battery longevity estimation is vital for their efficient operation, impacting decision-making and resource management. These robots adapt to changing conditions using machine learning techniques to optimize tasks, improve performance, and enhance efficiency. Widely used across sectors like healthcare, agriculture, and space, these systems benefit significantly from accurate energy management. While other machine learning models are effective for time-series data, they often require large datasets and extensive computational resources. Training deep learning models, in particular, is time-intensive and computationally expensive. Boosting algorithms, such as GBM, XGBoost, and AdaBoost, offer a more efficient solution by iteratively correcting errors and focusing on challenging cases, delivering better accuracy and computational efficiency for complex tasks like battery life prediction. This research applies Gradient Boosting Machines, XGBoost, and AdaBoost to predict battery life based on conditions and energy consumption. GBM combines decision trees, training each tree to address the errors of the previous one, while XGBoost enhances performance with faster and more efficient learning. AdaBoost uses simple decision trees to address misclassifications effectively. The models are evaluated for accuracy and efficiency, showcasing the potential of boosting algorithms to improve energy optimization in autonomous robots. This study highlights their capability to enhance predictive accuracy and optimize energy management across diverse sectors, ensuring more reliable autonomous operations. This advancement supports the development of more sustainable and efficient autonomous robotic systems.

articleTitle: Enhancing Intrusion Detection Systems through Federated Learning and Gated Recurrent Units
abstract: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) systems are essential for monitoring Critical Infrastructure (CI), such as Refineries, Pipelines, Power Grids and Mass Transport Systems. The interconnected nature of these systems and their associated networks are facing a wide range of cyber threats that pose a serious security threat. Recent research work has demonstrated Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) are effective in mitigating cyber-attacks. Therefore, this article proposes a novel approach to address cyber-attack detection in a critical infrastructure based on Federated-Gated Recurrent Units (FGRU). The proposed algorithm locally trains the GRU model on local data. Federated learning is a distributed machine learning technique, where multiple IoT devices prepare an on-device model training on device local data. Then these IoT devices send the model weights to central server. The federated structure allows data aggregation through multiple communication rounds over each local ICS channel, allowing for data privacy and confidentiality. The server aggregates these updates to improve the global model. The model performance in the paper is validated on real-world gas pipeline ICS data, making it suitable to apply on industrial scenarios.

articleTitle: Enabling Human-Machine Interfaces with 5G RedCap: Architecture, Key Requirements, and Challenges
abstract: G wireless communication protocols introduce a new paradigm for Human Machine Interface (HMI), allowing for a seamless user experience everywhere. HMI applications require low latency, balanced data rate, low energy consumption, and cost efficiency. The recent development of 3GPP-based $\mathbf{5 G}$ NR Reduced Capability (RedCap) may serve as the solution to fulfill this objective. This article focuses on the compatibility of the RedCap protocol with developing HMI. We have studied numerous previous research works by other authors related to the requirements of various HMI use cases and conducted a secondary study on how the capabilities of RedCap can satisfy these requrements. We examine the application cases of HMI, such as virtual reality (VR), augmented reality (AR), industrial collaborative robotics (Cobots), and wearables, as well as the RedCap requirements for HMI deployment. Furthermore, we discuss potential technological architectures and characteristics. Comparing the HMI link level requirements with the RedCap link level performance offerings, we observe that RedCap can be a suitable solution to meet the HMI communication demands. Finally, we discuss challenges and potential research directions for accomplishing this goal such as security, privacy, scalability, interoperability, and large level integration.

articleTitle: Architectural Adaptation for road humps detection in adverse light scenario
abstract: Road hump is a semi-cylindrical elevation on the road made across specific locations of the road. The vehicle needs to manoeuvre the hump by reducing the speed to avoid car damages and pass over the road hump safely. Road Humps on road surfaces if identified in advance helps to maintain the security and stability of vehicles, especially in adverse visibility condition viz. night scenarios. We have proposed a deep learning architecture adaptation by implementing MISH activation function and developing a new classification loss function called “Effective Focal Loss” for Indian road humps detection in adverse light scenario. We captured images comprising of marked and unmarked road humps from two different types of cameras across South India to build heterogeneous dataset. Heterogeneous dataset enabled the algorithm to train and improve the accuracy of detection. The images were pre-processed, annotated for two classes viz, marked hump and unmarked hump. The dataset from these images was used for training the single stage object detection algorithm. We utilised an algorithm to synthetically generate reduced visible road humps scenario. We observed that our proposed framework effectively detected the marked and unmarked hump in the images in clear and adverse light environment. This architectural adaptation sets up an option for early detection of Indian road humps in reduced visibility condition thereby enhancing the autonomous driving technology to handle wider range of real-world scenario.

articleTitle: Temporal Community Analysis Using Centrality Measures
abstract: This research explores temporal community detection to identify patterns in course grading and offerings at The University of Illinois from Spring 2010 to Spring 2020. Using a dataset that includes course grades, subject codes, instructors, and student enrolment, the study applies four community detection algorithms—Greedy Modularity, Louvain, Leiden, and Walktrap—to examine how courses group based on grading similarities over time. The data is pre-processed, split into time slices, and represented as graphs where nodes are courses and edges are weighted by cosine similarity of grading patterns. Key metrics such as modularity, community size, edge density, overlap, and persistence are used to evaluate algorithm performance. The results provide insights into the evolution of grading structures, course groupings, and instructional trends, offering a deeper understanding of the dynamics in educational data. This analysis contributes to improved decision-making in academic program development and resource allocation.

articleTitle: Predictive Modeling of Metastatic Diagnosis Period in Breast Cancer using Machine Learning
abstract: The objective of this research is to utilize machine learning models to forecast the period of metastatic diagnosis in breast cancer patients, with a specific focus on triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) data sourced from the WiDS Datathon 2024 dataset, which includes 19,000 records. This dataset encompasses a wide range of medical and socioeconomic variables that play a crucial role in comprehending healthcare disparities. Our assessment encompassed models such as Random Forest, XGBoost, and Support Vector Regression, with the Gradient Boosting Regressor (GBR) emerging as the most precise, achieving a Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 80.685. An analysis of feature importance revealed that the breast cancer diagnosis code, patient age, and geographic location (zip3) were the most significant predictors. Although feature importance was lower, payer type and socioeconomic factors also contributed to the model’s predictive capabilities. This study underscores the capacity of machine learning to capture both major and minor influences on metastatic diagnosis, thereby assisting in early detection and enhancing treatment strategies for TNBC patients.

articleTitle: Integrating Transformative AI for Next-Level Predictive Analytics in Healthcare
abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in healthcare has facilitated new predictive analytics, assisting clinicians in making more accurate decisions based on data, rather than guessing. This particular study intends to assess the implementation of AI-based predictive models into the Health Information Exchange (HIE) systems to improve the clinical practice as well as the decision-making processes within health practitioners. Using HIE networks’ various datasets, we constructed and tested neural networks, decision trees, and ensemble methods machine learning algorithms that were developed for accurate clinical predictions. A comprehensive analysis of data preprocessing and testing was performed to ensure quality and consistency yielding models that were quite coherent. The results conclude that patient outcomes can be enhanced by applying AI integrated Predictive models and that focus on targeted intervention programs and monitoring disease progression can be achieved. These findings suggest the promise of advanced AI models combined with HIE systems for generating useful real-time decision-making information and effective healthcare personalized care pathways. This study forms the basis for more work using AI in clinical settings and makes a case for AI use across a wider healthcare setting.

articleTitle: Privacy Preservation And Performance Improvement of HealthCare Data Prediction and Storage Using Map-Reduce Framework
abstract: Big data is observed as the state-of-the-art-concern which is employed to deal with immense range of data in definite fields like remote sensing, medical, customer services and so on. In recent days, health care industry has been originating vast expansion to develop individual specialized techniques. After all it is mandatory to protect the confidential patient’s medical record as it is stored in the untrusted cloud which in turn continual to concede with users according to their requirements. Despite, sustaining the ownership of an entire medical records is the crucial issueamong patient and the hospital thereby the primary responsibility of the hospital is to maintain the records precisely. Hence, the medical records of patients are not only accessed in any emergency issues or treatment. Furthermore, Big Data classification is typically a tiresome and extended task. The Map Reduce Framework technique offers the processing of data which is being paralleled through the distribution of data in smaller chunks over clusters. The technique of Map Reduce is being presented which is utilized for processing data items that are heterogeneous. By means of the well-known framework Map reduce issues and challengesof existing methods could be solved randomly. This research paper attempts pragmatic method of disease prediction and classification using discrete multilayer perceptron-based classification. Subsequently, the proposed technique performs preprocessing using Normalization, Adaptive Shearlet polynomial component analysis-based features extraction, optimization of extracted features using recurrent chicken swarm optimization algorithm, classification and prediction. Ultimately, the medical information is stored in cloud server byperforming encryption to the data using semantic polynomial based blowfish encryption
